articleTitle: A Low-Area High-Precision 100 MSPS 9-Bit Current-Steering DAC In 130nm BiCOMS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a 9-bit binary-coded current-Steering Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC), which is designed using 130 nm SiGe BiCOMS process. The sampling rate is set to be 100 MSPS. Cadence Spectre is used to simulate static and dynamic error indicators to evaluate the performance of the DAC circuit. Simulation results show that the Differential Nonlinearity (DNL) is ±0.15 LSB and Integral Nonlinearity (INL) is ± 0.44 LSB, indicating high accuracy and excellent static performance. Additionally, the circuit has a low static power consumption of 3.6 mW. The Effective Number of Bits (ENOB) is maintained 8.74 at a sampling rate of 100 MSPS. The die area is only about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.033 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: An Improved Cascoded Ring Amplifier Based Pipelined-SAR ADC with a Continuous Time Second Stage
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a ring amplifier based pipelined-SAR analog-to-digital converter (ADC). In advanced technology, the ring amplifier's three-stage inverter provides limited gain, so the self-biased cascoded output stage is designed to enhance the gain of the ring amplifier. In addition, a continuous time SAR is adopted to speed up the second stage, which improves the power efficiency and is not affected by the frequency of the input signal. This ADC is completed with a 28 nm CMOS process. The 12-bit ADC achieves 64.1 dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion-ratio (SNDR) at a Nyquist input, with a sampling rate of 250 MS/s and a power consumption of 0.8 mW.

articleTitle: Implementation of Brushless DC Motor Control Chip Based on PWM Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a brushless DC motor control chip based on PWM technique is proposed. It integrates the rotor position decoder and includes functions for forward and reverse rotation as well as angle selection. The chip integrates the functions of under-voltage protection, over-current protection, and over-temperature protection. This integration enhances the functionality of the chip. The width of the PWM signals is controlled by an external modulation input voltage. Motor speed is controlled by generating a PWM signal with a variable pulse width. The chip outputs six control signals that can be used to control a three-phase brushless motor. The chip design is completed using a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.25\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> BCD process, and the simulation and test results are consistent. The chip is easy to control, occupies a small area, and can reliably drive and control the motor.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Lightweight CNN Acceleration System for Real-Time Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In recent years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become the core of many artificial intelligence applications, especially in fields such as image recognition and speech recognition. Deploying convolutional neural networks in hardware, as opposed to software, can increase speed and reduce power consumption. In this article, we propose an FPGA-based convolutional neural network acceleration system. This system optimizes LeNet-5 into a lightweight convolutional neural network model by replacing traditional convolution with depthwise separable convolutions and reducing the number of fully connected layers. After designing a parallel processing scheme for the computation process of the model, a CNN acceleration IP core is implemented using Verilog and applied to real-time handwritten digit recognition. This system can recognize one frame of image in 326.24µs, which is approximately 1s faster than CPU recognition. The total power consumption of the entire system is 1.947W, meeting the requirements of high real-time performance and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Determination of Lead and Cadmium Ions Using Gold Nanoparticles Modified Screen-Printed Graphene Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work is aimed at improving the sensing performance of screen-printed graphene electrodes (SPGEs) to detect heavy metal ions. A simple electrochemical method for depositing gold nanoparticles on the SPGEs is presented in this paper. The modification on the electrode surface was characterized by means of scanning electron microscopy and energy dispersive spectroscopy. The electrochemical performance of the modified electrodes was evaluated by cyclic voltammetry and square wave anodic stripping voltammetry. Experimental results show that the electrochemical response of the SPGEs has been significantly improved by the modification of gold nanoparticles. The modified electrodes exhibit promising application for the detection of Pb(II) and Cd(II) ions in water.

articleTitle: A Configurable Computing Architecture for Split-Radix FFT
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Image recovery algorithms applied to imaging systems such as lensless imaging in end devices are a high-speed edge computing process. Diffraction recovery algorithms typically include operations such as FFT/IFFT, amplitude constraint, phase constraint, and intensity operations. FFT/IFFT, as the main operation in these algorithms, is usually computed using the butterfly algorithm, which can be categorized into three main types: single-base algorithm, mixed-radix algorithm, and split-radix algorithm. To meet the hardware resource constraints of edge devices, this paper proposes a configurable computing architecture for the SRFFT algorithm by analyzing the specific butterfly unit structures. Using mode control signals, the architecture can be configured into three modes: basic butterfly unit computation, 8-point tail computation, and 2-point tail computation. By reusing the underlying floating-point computation units, the proposed architecture not only computes the FFT efficiently compared to other split-radix algorithms but also further reduces the utilization of the underlying computational resources, making it highly suitable for edge devices with limited resources.

articleTitle: A Bandgap Reference with 3.2 ppm/°C TC, 587.2pV Noise and 48dB PSRR at 1MHz
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article presents a bandgap reference circuit with high precision, low noise, and high power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) for the low DC supply noise. Employing a segmented curvature compensation technique, the positive and negative temperature coefficient can be adjusted, effectively minimizing the temperature drift of the reference voltage. A temperature-robust pseudo-resistor capacitor filter is utilized to eliminate mid-frequency power supply ripple and noise. Furthermore, a fast start-up circuit (FSC) substantially reduces the start-up time. Simulation results within the -40°C to 135°C temperature range can keep a stable 1.11V and reveal a best-case bandgap temperature coefficient of 3.2ppm/°C across all process corners and three supply voltages. The circuit's start-up time is approximately 6uS with a worst-case output noise of 587. 2p V at 1MHz and PSRR maintains over 48dB at 1MHz, demonstrating effective noise and ripple suppression capability.

articleTitle: 2.5D Interposer HBM Signal Integrity Analysis Based on Fast MoM
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) placed side-by-side with ASIC on silicon interposer is capable of delivering the TB/s bandwidth. To maintain such high bandwidth, it is crucial to perform extensive signal integrity analysis and optimization. In this paper, a novel methodology for fast HBM signal integrity analysis and optimization is proposed, which includes accurate HBM channel model extraction and fast HBM channel simulation in both frequency domain and time domain with IBIS-AMI models to ultimately enable full signal coverage with automation.

articleTitle: A 3-GS/s 12-Bit Time-Interleaved Wideband Pipeline ADC Using Sample-and-Hold Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 3-GS/s 12-bit two-channel time-interleaved analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is described in this paper. The ADC employs two sample-and-holding amplifiers (SHAs) at the front end, which drive two pipeline sub-ADCs to interleave samples to achieve a 3 GS/s sampling rate. The SHA with 1.5x gain can relax the linearity requirement of the input buffer and ensure sufficient input amplitude for the subsequent sub-ADC. The front-end bandwidth of the ADC presented in this paper reaches up to 6 GHz. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, the prototype ADC achieves an outstanding SNDR of 53.71 dB at 3 GS/s with a 1.227 GHz input. The ADC core area is 1.66 mm-, including the digital part, the power consumption is 1408 mW.

articleTitle: An Computing-in-Memory SAD Architecture Capable of Realizing High-Precision Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper describes a computing in memory array based on 10T SRAM cells for realizing the subtraction operation of 8bit inputs with 8bit weights in SAD operations, and it is able to achieve high discharge linearity by improving its discharge and high and low-bit merging methods for 10T SRAM arrays. The design and simulation of the memory array part of this architecture is carried out in 110nm CMOS process with a supply voltage of 1.2 V. The simulation results show that the memory array has good linearity of 99.66%, which is conducive to the realization of high-precision SAD operations in the subsequent CIM system.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Inverted-T SSOI FinFET for RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, the analog and RF performance of inverted-T FinFET (IT-FinFET) transistor are investigated using TCAD simulation. Compared with 14 nm FinFET, the device increases the channel width under a given layout area, so that the on-current increases by about 300 %. The electrostatic control capability is optimized by adjusting the device structure. The work functions of SOI region and fin region of the device are respectivelyset to make threshold voltages of horizontal and vertical channels consistent. reduces the subthreshold slope (SS) to 73.3 mV/decade. We have used strained Siicon as material for the device to further increase the on-current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_{on})$</tex> and trans-conductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(G_{m})$</tex>. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_{m}$</tex> is increasd to 0.35 mSum. Thanks to the Inverted-T structure, the cut-off frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{T})$</tex> increases 10 %, mainly due to increase in transconductance and decrease parasitic capacitance. Without the backgate bias, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{T}$</tex> achieves 389 GHz. Additionally, as the backgate voltage is incremented to 2 V, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{T}$</tex> increases to 397 GHz.

articleTitle: A Harmonic-Rejection Radio Frequency Transmitter Employing 33%-Duty-Cycle LO Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper reports a SAW-less RF transmitter that proposes a third harmonic suppression technique by employing 33<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>-duty-cycle local oscillator (LO) waveforms. Besides, it employs a N-path switched-capacitor (SC) mixer, providing a high Q bandpass filtering at different RF to achieve a good compromise between output power and linearity. The gain provided by a transconductor (gm) could not only compensate for attenuation caused by 3fLo-suppression but also enhance out-of-band (OB) noise rejection effectively. An auxiliary gm is introduced to improve the linearity of the power amplifier (PA) driver. Simulated in 65nm CMOS process, our transmitter manifests good linearity (CIM3 <-52dBc) under 2.2dBm output power. The OB noise is <-155.5dBc/Hz. The transmitter consumes 118mW power. The active area is 0.075 mnm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Cubic Voltage Generation Circuit for Low-Phase Noise ATCXO Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A high order voltage generation circuit based on the parallel structure of differential amplifiers is introduced by studying the compensated voltage generation module in ATCXO. Unlike the traditional Gilbert multiplier cascade structure, this method effectively reduces the step-by-step amplification of noise in the circuit, thus significantly improving the phase noise performance. At the same time, the whole module can be realized with only twenty to thirty active and passive devices, without unique processes, which can simultaneously achieve low-power and low-cost design based on effective noise reduction and is more conducive to on-chip implementation. In this way, a high order voltage generation circuit is designed for a low-phase noise ATCXO. The ATCXO designed using this method has a frequency stability of ±2.2ppm and a phase noise of -133.2dBc/Hz @ 1kHz within the temperature range of -40°C to 80°C. The chip area of the high order voltage generation circuit module is 0.47×0.25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Low Energy BFSK Receiver with Adaptive Clock-less Digital Demodulation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article presents an energy-efficient binary frequency shift keying (BFSK) receiver supporting 915MHz for wireless body area networks (WBAN) applications. The proposed receiver implemented in the 55nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology with IV supply. An improved passive mixer is proposed to reduce power consumption while providing gain. The proposed receiver employs an adaptive clock-less demodulation method, enabling fast demodulation of the required data at a rate of 5Mb/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> with a latency of only 184ns. The receiver consumes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$448\text{pW}$</tex>, corresponding to an energy consumption of 89.6pJ per received bit.

articleTitle: A High-Octave UWB LNA with a Positive Slope Gain by Using Current Reuse Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance GaAs low-noise amplifier (LNA) designed for wideband applications spanning from 1 GHz to 9 GHz. The LNA exhibits consistent positive slope gain characteristics across a range of operating temperatures, including −40°C, +25°C, and +85°C. Measured gain values are stable within a robust 24 to 27.5 dB window. With an impressively low noise figure (NF) of no more than 1.4 dB, the amplifier maintains excellent signal integrity. Its output power at 1 dB compression point (OP1dB) exceeds 13.3 dBm, while the third-order intercept point (OIP3) is greater than 25.5 dBm, indicating strong linearity and dynamic range. The LNA demonstrates superior matching performance and operates with a quiescent current of 42 to 44 mA under a supply voltage of 5V. Notably, the compact chip footprint measures just 1.8 mm x 1.1 mm, making it ideal for space-constrained systems.

articleTitle: A Design of Ultra-Wide Band Six-Bit Digital Attenuator with Low Phase Shift
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband six-bit digital attenuator operating at frequencies ranging from DC to 40 GHz was designed and implemented in 0.15 µm GaAs pHEMT process. The control level of This six-bit attenuator is 0/-5 V, and achieves a step attenuation of 0.5 dB and a dynamic attenuation range of 31.5 dB. The attenuator circuit is composed of six basic attenuation units cascaded. In the design of large attenuation bit, a simple T -type structure which is opposite to the phase change trend of the original structure is added, so that the full state attenuation phase variation can be less than ±8.4°, which solves the problem of large additional phase shift in the high frequency part of UWB, the insertion loss is less than 5.5 dB, the root-mean-square of attenuation error from DC to 35 GHz is less than 1.6 dB. The chip size is 2.4 mmx0.7mmx0.1 mm.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Low-Ripple Buck DC-DC Converter Based on Module Reuse
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on double comparators and several digital units, a buck DC-DC converter is implemented in 65-nm CMOS. The switching frequency is automatic sliding from dozen kHz to sub-MHz for different load conditions. Simulated results show that the presented DC-DC converter achieve a peak-to-peak ripple voltage smaller than 2.55 mV, with the switching frequency of 18–526 kHz. The proposed DC-DC converter also has a high efficiency up to 94%, with the supply voltage of 1.8-3.3 V, the output voltage of 1.2-1.8 V, and the load current of 1–50 mA. The presented converter benefits low complexity, high efficiency, and low ripple with a module-reuse scheme, which combines the error comparator with the peak-voltage one by using digital switches.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Low-current-Mismatch PFD+CP Circuit for 11.3G CPPLL Application
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Combination circuit of PFD and CP was designed using 65nm CMOS technology to achieve low jitter and high frequency. Some techniques, such as TSPC, cascade structure and gain enhancement technology, can be employed into PFD and CP to suppress unfavorable factors, such as charge sharing, current mismatch, leakage current, etc. Simulation results show that the variation of voltage is almost linear and the basic invariable control voltage in the transient process, showing that it cannot also introduce the significant frequency jitter. CP current matching accuracy is about 0.047% in the range of 0.35V~0.8V and the maximum total leakage current in the range of 0V~l.2V is 23.3pA, which can effectively be reduced to improve jitter performance.

articleTitle: A Floating Peak Current Detection and Protection Circuit with Current Compensation, Dual Opening Mechanism and Negative Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Traditional circuits often suffer from significant peak current fluctuations due to sensitivity to temperature, process variations, and other conditions, leading to detection deviations that can damage the circuit. This paper presents the design of a peak current detection and protection circuit for a BUCK DC-DC converter. A current compensation structure is proposed to reduce peak current fluctuations, ensuring the desired peak current is achieved. This implementation uses different proportions of positive and negative temperature coefficient resistors to control branch current changes due to temperature and provide current compensation. Additionally, a dual opening mechanism is employed. The high-side switch transistor is activated only when both the external control signal and the floating voltage conditions are simultaneously met, ensuring the proper response of the circuit's floating logic. As a result, the inductor is charged, the inductor's current rises, and peak current detection begins. The detection mechanism continuously monitors current changes throughout the process. When the current reaches the preset peak, logic signals control the high-side switch transistor to turn off, preventing further current increase and ensuring the converter circuit operates within the normal current range. Given that the left end of the inductor is at a floating potential, a level shift circuit is designed to switch the voltage between floating and ground logic, also serving as a negative feedback control logic. This circuit is implemented using a 180 nm BCD process. Simulation results show that, with an input voltage of 18 V, the circuit detects a stable peak current of 3.9 A, and logic signals control the circuit switching state to prevent further current increase, thereby achieving the goal of protecting the circuit.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Broadband Quadrature Signal Generation Circuit Based on 130nm BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a high-precision wideband quadrature signal generation circuit is implemented based on 130nm BiCMOS. The circuit is composed of two three-stage polyphase filters, a buffer amplifier added between the two polyphase filters to compensate for the loss and a limiting amplifier at the end. In the range of 0.4GHz-8GHz, the phase error between the I channel and Q channel signals is less than 0.3° and the amplitude error of that is less than 0.005dB. The DC power consumption of the circuit is 667. 9m Wand the chip area of chip is 1.32mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband Bonding Wire Interconnection Compensation Structure for W Band Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this article, a novel wideband millimeter-wave interconnection solution for integrated circuit (IC) to Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) board using bonding wire has been developed. In the W band, high impedance transmission lines require finer line width requirements, which combine with a series of low impedance transmission lines to form a filter matching network to reduce the parasitic effects of bonding wire. However, limitations in manufacturing requirement are wider than 60um transmission lines to improve manufacturability, so it is difficult to achieve the high impedance transmission lines in W band. By introducing defected ground structure (DGS) under coplanar waveguide with backside ground (CPWG) transmission lines in four-layer LCP substrate, the high impedance transmission lines can be easily obtained without the additional process requirements. In addition, the bonding wire compensation structure uses single bonding wire to reduce the technical difficulty in bonding process and save the bonding cost. The test results show that the structure has a good transmission performance ranging from 75 to 110GHz with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> better than −10.97dB and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> less than −2.98dB.

articleTitle: A Wide Input Range, High Power Supply Rejection Bandgap Voltage Reference with Exponential Curvature-Compensate
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a wide input range, low temperature coefficient (TC), high power supply rejection (PSR) bandgap voltage reference (BGR) for low dropout regulators (LDO) is proposed. This performance is achieved by introducing a pre-regulator circuit, a PSR enhancement stage and an exponential curvature-compensation structure. The bandgap voltage reference is implemented in SMIC 0.18-µm BCD process. Simulation results show that at supply voltages ranging from 4V to 20V, the reference voltage is 1.206V, the temperature coefficient is 5.016ppm/°C, the power supply rejection is −101dB at 1KHz, and the linear regulation ratio is 21.4µV/V.

articleTitle: Effect of Sc Concentration on the Memory Window in Al1-xScxN/Two-Dimensional Channel Ferroelectric Field-Effect Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Recently, the integration of a scandium-doped aluminum nitride (Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>N) dielectric layer with a two-dimensional (2D) channel has attracted significant attention in ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs). The effect of Sc doping concentrations (x) on the memory window (MW) in FeFETs with a 100 nm Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>N dielectric layer and a 2D MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> channel is investigated using the technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations. Simulation results show that the MW increases from 34.23 V to 39.08 V with increasing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> from 0.27 to 0.36, and then decreases to 31.07 V as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> further increases to 0.43. Furthermore, the MW gradually becomes symmetrical at about a gate voltage of 0 V as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> increases from 0.27 to 0.43. These variations in the MW are mainly attributed to the decrease of coercive field (Ec) with increasing x, which will enhance the switching of ferroelectric polarization. This work offers valuable insights into optimizing the MW for Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>N FeFETs.

articleTitle: A Bandpass Filter with Bootstrapped Source Terminal and Employing Bias Voltage on Gate of Pseudo Resistor for Bio-Signal Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The integrated bandpass filter (BPF) within bio-signal sensing systems forms the critical element for signal detection and pre-processing. This paper presents a BPF with the proposed bootstrapped source terminals of the transistors within the pseudo resistor (PR) and employing an external bias voltage on gates of PR (BSVG-PR), to enhance the impedance of PR and lower the high-pass cut-off frequency. The BPF with BSVG-PR dynamically supports lower biomedical and neural signal sensing. The proposed circuit is designed in a 0.18-µm CMOS process. The proposed BPF with BSVG-PR occupies die areas of 0.008 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and achieves high-pass cut-off frequencies of circa 1.0 mHz.

articleTitle: Automatic Routing Algorithm for Differential Pair and Current Mirror in Analog Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Differential pairs and current mirrors are basic building blocks in analog circuits. Routing is a crucial part of circuit design and directly determines circuits' performance. Existing papers on routing of analog circuits mostly use one fixed combination of metal layers and the placement is fixed. Such approach may result in wasted chip area and high production cost. This paper proposes an algorithm which can route differential pair and current mirror in flexible metal layer combinations, to be selected by designers. This algorithm considers routing symmetry, electro migration (EM) and voltage (IR) drop. It also adopts channel multiplexing and can adjust the row spacing of placement according to routing plan. Therefore, it effectively utilizes chip area and reduces cost. In addition, our algorithm automatically performs statistics on routing related data, making it easier to evaluate routing quality. The routing results show that under various metal layer combinations, our algorithm can successfully achieve high-quality routing for differential pair and current mirror with various placement forms.

articleTitle: Secure Encryption and Decryption Circuit on 8T1C Structure-Based Charge Accumulation and Dissipation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: To solve the large resource overhead and risk problems of traditional encryption and decryption technologies. This paper presents a secure computing scheme of 8T1C structure based on charge accumulation and dissipation which is used to implement low-cost encryption and decryption circuits. Firstly, the scheme uses the characteristics of capacitor charge accumulation and dissipation to complete the XOR encryption. Decryption of data is performed by dynamically charging and discharging the load capacitor. Secondly the 8T1C SRAM unit structure is designed in combination with the Static Random-Access Memory Physical Unclonable Function (SRAM PUF) structure. The encryption and decryption operations are built into the storage unit to reduce the hardware resource overhead, by integrating additional MOS tubes and capacitors. Finally, the encrypted data is reshaped by the sense amplifier and stored in the same unit. The function of safe data storage is realized through hardware reuse of circuit resources. The security encryption and decryption circuit is simulated and verified In the TSMC 65nm process. The experimental results show that the designed encryption and decryption circuit structure can confuse the traces of the original data and recover the original information content in the decryption process. PUF key uniqueness is 50.31%, randomness is 99.9%, and it has passed the NIST randomness test. Under the working environment of -50 °C~125°C and 0.8V to 1.5V, the worst bit error rate is 7.6%, which can be applied to the security encryption field of the Internet of Things.

articleTitle: A 760uW 1.83GHz PLL Using a Single-Ring Oscillator-Based Integrator with Background Frequency Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A phase-locked loop (PLL) utilizing a single ring oscillator-based integrator and background frequency calibration is presented. The in-band phase noise and power efficiency of the PLL are improved by introducing an integrator based on a single ring oscillator. By employing background frequency calibration, the PLL demonstrates robustness against process, supply voltage, and temperature variations. In addition, a source-switched charge pump with reverse sub-threshold leakage current suppression are used to improve reference spur. Designed in 55 nm CMOS process, the PLL has a power consumption of 760 uW at 1 V supply voltage, a phase noise of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$111 \text{dBc} / \text{Hz}$</tex> at an offset frequency of 1 MHz, and a lock time of less than 0.8us.

articleTitle: A Precision Wideband Quadrature Signal Generation Using 130nm SiGe BiCMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A quadrature generation circuit designed to convert local oscillator signals into quadrature signals is described. An RC polyphase filter construction produces precise I/Q quadrature signals over a very wide frequency range. The phase correction circuit features a tuning range of 3 degrees, and limiting amplifiers are employed to calibrate the amplitude imbalance of the I/Q signals. Implemented in the 130nm SiGe BiCMOS process, the phase generation circuit operates within a frequency range of 400 MHz to 8 GHz, achieving a quadrature phase inaccuracy of under 0.4 degrees and an I/Q amplitude imbalance of less than 0.1 dB.

articleTitle: A Low-power High-precision Differential Output 13bit R-2R DAC Pathway in 180nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 13bit R-2R DAC pathway is implemented in 180nm CMOS. This pathway transforms single-ended digital control words into positive and negative analog voltage outputs, with the capability to alter the polarity of the differential output voltages. The R-2R DAC circuit serves as the core component in the DAC pathway, exhibiting integral nonlinearity errors (INL) and differential nonlinearity errors (DNL) of 0.575 LSB and 0.34 LSB, respectively. It achieves an Effective Number of Bits (ENOB) of 12.87 bits, a Spurious-Free Dynamic Range (SFDR) of 87.39 dB, and a Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of -84.47 dB. This DAC pathway is characterized by low power consumption of 0.722 mW and high output voltage accuracy, achieving output voltage error of 1.5%.

articleTitle: A Single-Channel 2-GS/s 8-bit Two-Step SAR ADC in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a single-channel 8-bit 2 GS/s two-step successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). Combined with the passive residue transfer and comparators alternation technology, the proposed SAR ADC is currently one of the fastest single-channel 8-bit SAR ADCs, and its performance is superior to time-interleaved SAR ADCs at the same resolution and sampling rate. The proposed ADC in 28-nm CMOS consumes 6.91 mW at 2 GS/s with a 1V supply. It achieves a Nyquist SNDR of 45.6 dB and results in an FoM of 22.2 fJ/conv.-step.

articleTitle: A Fault Simulation Based Functional Safety Platform for Automotive Chips Complying with ISO26262
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the increasing scale of automotive electronics and the gradual maturity of the automotive-grade chip development process, simulation-level fault injection has become the most mainstream fault injection method in the industry. In this paper, a fault injection platform closely coupled with FMEDA based on the Verilog programming interface (VPI) is proposed to solve the functional safety simulation requirements of the ISO26262 for automotive-grade chips at the RT level and GL level. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed platform, a memory protected by CRC has been used for experiment.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Wideband Low Noise Amplifier with Excellent Port Matching and Gain Flatness
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A design method of ultra-wideband three-stage Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) using 65nm CMOS technology is presented in this paper. Gm-boost technique is used to suppress the drain noise of the common-gate (CG) transistor in the first-stage. The gain peaking frequency of each stage's amplifier is suitably adjusted to realize excellent gain flatness. Inductive feed-forward technique is introduced to achieve broadband input matching and to make the layout more compact. In the post simulation, the proposed LNA achieves 3.7-5.7dB Noise Figure (NF) across 12.7GHz to 49.8GHz bandwidth, with Sll<-10dB, S22<-14dB, and S21=11.0-12.7dB. The LNA consumes 25.7mW dc power, and occupies 0.27mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> core area.

articleTitle: Memristive Chaotic Circuit Designed for Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Memristor is a device with nonlinear and memory characteristics, and it is an appropriate candidate for constructing chaotic and hyperchaotic systems. In this work, we have designed a memristor model and subsequently built a memristor chaotic circuit. The basic dynamic behavior of the system with varying the circuit parameters was studied in detail by using the traditional nonlinear analysis method. In addition, the memristive chaotic system also has the advantages of being extremely sensitive to system parameters, initial conditions and unpredictability, aperiodicity and structural complexity. The successful application of such design on image encryption and decryption with high security was eventually demonstrated.

articleTitle: Structural Optimization Design and Simulation of a Novel Chip Level Electroosmotic Micromixer
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that a variety of samples to be tested can be mixed efficiently and quickly, a new structure optimization design scheme of chip level electroosmotic micromixe with obstacle arrays and considering electroosmotic effect is proposed. Firstly, the chip level electroosmotic micromixer is modeled and simulated. Secondly, the mixing performance of chip level micromixers with obstacle array under the condition of non-electro osmotic and electroosmotic conditions is discussed. Finally, the parameters such as different shapes, different diameters, different lateral spacing and different electric field intensity of obstacle array in the chip level electro osmotic micromixer are simulated and analyzed. The simulation results show that the chip level electro osmotic micromixer is under the condition that the obstacle shape is circular, the diameter is 200 um, the lateral spacing is 300 um, and the electric field intensity applied by the AC electric field is ± 20V. the mixing efficiency index of the chip level electro osmotic micromixer is 45.23 % higher than that of the chip level non-electro osmotic micromixer with the same obstacle parameters, which enables a variety of samples to be tested to achieve efficient and rapid micro mixing.

articleTitle: A Bandwidth-Adaptive On-Chip Storage Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A scalable bandwidth-adaptive on-chip storage network architecture is proposed to address the severe data conflict and low bus parallelism in existing multi-level storage, Crossbar, and NoC architectures in edge accelerated computing. This architecture combines the advantages of centralized and distributed memory, allowing the memory hierarchy to be flexibly adapted based on current computational needs and memory access patterns to better accommodate multi-core processors and parallel computing requirements. This paper designs the result visualization method to visualize the stress of storing each node and bus. Furthermore, the full path test incentive is intended for the secondary sharing policy and router. The feasibility of this paper's architecture is verified through VCS simulation and visualization analysis.

articleTitle: A Study on Semiconductor Device Training Using Digital-Twins and Solid-edge
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this study, we introduce an educational course for training the semiconductor device. The course is divided into two primary sections: a virtual space created through Digital-Twin and Solid-edge for 3D reverse engineering. We made the semiconductor device in the Digital Twin environment using Unity. This device can be inspected from various perspectives. Using the mock-up and model inside the Digital-Twin as reference, we can reverse engineer the device using Solid-edge. Once the reverse engineering process is completed, we can redesign or resize the device for testing experiments. Finally, the reverse-engineered device can be 3D-printed to verify the results. Through these processes, we aim to provide students with hands-on experience and enhance their understanding of equipment operation and design.

articleTitle: An Antenna Tuning Switch with Novel Resistor Chain Bias Network to Enhance Power Handling Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis and design of a novel bias network for high power antenna tuner switch to enhance power handling capability which improve the limitation of breakdown voltage from the unequally voltage drop among the stacked field effect transistors (FETs). A simplified equivalent model for OFF -state of a switch is established and a bias network with resistor chain structure is then proposed to achieve uniform voltage distribution across the stacked FETs. Based on the proposed method, a single-pole single-throw (SPST) antenna tuning switch is designed and fabricated in 0.13 µm radio frequency silicon-on-insulator CMOS technology. Simulation and measurement results show that the switch features a uniform voltage distribution and a significant improvement on breakdown voltage (BV) by 20 V.

articleTitle: Design of a Capacitance Measurement Circuit and System with Parasitic Capacitance Elimination
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the application system of capacitive sensors, the capacitance values of these sensors are generally small. It is crucial to remove the influence of parasitic capacitance. In order to achieve this goal, this paper introduces a capacitance time conversion measurement circuit and system that remove parasitic capacitance. The capacitance value is indirectly measured by the time when the capacitor is charged. The entire measurement circuit includes an MCU core, I/O with pull-up resistor, TDC (Time to Digital Converter) to count the charging time, MCU commands to switch the measurement mode, and calculates the measurement results to eliminate the influence of parasitic capacitance. The measurement results presented in the article show that parasitic capacitance can almost completely be eliminated. This method can be applied to various capacitance measurement scenarios.

articleTitle: High-Voltage Silicon PIN Radiation Detectors with Trenched Field Limiting Ring
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, the trenched field limiting ring structure for PIN radiation detectors is proposed and studied. The impact of trench depth and width on the breakdown voltage is investigated through simulation. It is found that the breakdown voltage is 907.6V when the trench width is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, which indicates that dead area effect can be effectively decreased by reducing the field limiting ring width without lowering the breakdown voltage.

articleTitle: A Fully Integrated Low Noise and High Accuracy Low-Dropout Regulator in 130nm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this work, a method for obtaining an LDO with low output noise is proposed by applying a bandgap reference source that does not contain an operational amplifier and uses all triodes. In the bandgap reference source, an additional loop is used to achieve the effect of clamping the voltage. In the core circuit, a buffer and a pole tracking circuit are used to achieve a balance between high loop gain, stability and load transient response. An off-chip capacitor-free LDO is designed using the proposed methodology with SiGe 130 nm BiCMOS process. The design has a noise of 1.16 µV at 10 Hz and an integrated noise of 23.7 µV rms over the frequency range of 10 Hz ~ 100 MHz. The LDO has a small output capacitance of 20 pF and a quiescent current of only 400 µA.

articleTitle: An ALU Digital Backend Design Based on 90nmCNTFET Process
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As silicon-based integrated circuits scale down to dimensions below 65nm, they experience significant drawbacks such as severe leakage current and short-channel effects. Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistors (CNTFET) have emerged as a promising alternative for future integrated circuits due to their extremely small size, ultra-high carrier mobility, and quasi-one-dimensional ballistic transport properties. The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is a crucial component of processors and a focal point of research and development. This paper presents the design of an ALU based on the 90nmCNTFET Process Design Kit (PDK) developed by our research group. The ALU is capable of performing 12 functions, including addition, subtraction, and shifting operations. The digital backend design was completed using Innovus and compared to the TSMC90nm technology. The 90nm CNTFET-based ALU demonstrated a power consumption of 0.559mW, a delay of 1.188ns, and a power-delay product of 0.664pJ. The total layout area was 200µm × 200µm. The power-delay product of the 90nmCNTFET ALU shows an improvement over the ALU designed with TSMC90nm technology.

articleTitle: A 5.8-GHz High-Efficiency Inverse Class-F Rectifier Circuit with GaN Schottky Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a high-efficiency 5.8GHz inverse class-F rectifier for wireless power transmission (WPT). The rectifier is based on gallium nitride Schottky barrier diodes (GaN SBD) and consists of an input matching network, a harmonic control network and a DC-pass filter. The harmonic control network uses three microstrip lines to suppress the second and third harmonics, and shapes the voltage and current waveforms at both ends of the diode to reduce diode losses. The DC-pass filter at the output suppresses the fundamental, second and third harmonics. The measurements indicate that the rectifier implemented has an RF-DC conversion efficiency of 81.9% at an input power of 29 dBm. Additionally, it achieves an efficiency of over 70% in the power range of 19 dBm to 33 dBm, with a size of 28mm°23 mm.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Strong-Weak PUF Against Machine Learning Attacks with High Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Physical Unclonable Function (PUF), as a lightweight hardware security primitive, is widely applied in resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices. However, the strong PUFs are vulnerable to modeling attacks. In this paper, we propose a configurable hybrid strong-weak PUF (SW PUF) structure that combines the characteristics of strong with weak PUFs, which integrates both strong and weak PUFs into a new PUF design. This proposed SW PUF can be flexibly configured into a strong PUF (an arbiter PUF, a ring oscillator PUF, or a bistable ring PUF) or a weak PUF (SRAM PUF) which is configured by utilizing challenges to select different process biases. Moreover, the presented PUF utilizes unique key streams of weak PUF to bitwise encrypt the raw challenges from the strong PUFs to obfuscate the relationship between the challenge and the response, facilitating an inherent immunity to white-box modeling attacks. Experimental results show that the modeling accuracies of LR, SVM, CMA-ES, and ANN are close to 55% and the SW PUF has high reliability without any post-processing techniques.

articleTitle: A 12b 400MS/s 4-Time Interleaved Pipelined-SAR ADC with Fully Differential Bias-enhanced Ring Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 12-bit 400MS/s 4-channel time-interleaved pipelined-SAR ADC with a fully differential bias-enhanced ring amplifier for low-power and high-speed application is presented. The sub-ADC adopts a two-stage pipeline quantization scheme with a 6-bit SAR ADC in the first stage and a 7-bit SAR ADC in the second stage with 1-hit overlapping. To further optimize the speed of the sub-ADCs, a bias-enhanced ring amplifier is proposed. A prototype ADC is designed and simulated in 65nm CMOS technology with a standard 1.2 V supply voltage. With the least-mean-square algorithm calibration, this ADC achieves SNDR of 64.5 dB and SFDR of 86.6 dB. The whole ADC consumes 10.3mW, achieving a FoM of 19.9 fJ/conv-step.

articleTitle: A High dv/dt Immunity Complementary Current Compensation Level Shift Circuit for GaN Half-Bridge
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A novel complementary current compensation level shift circuit is proposed to cope with the dv/dt problem in the GaN half-bridge structure. The level shift circuit converts the input voltage of 0~5V to the output voltage of 35 ~ 40V. It uses a 40V HVMOS to realize the signal conversion, which is based on the current mirror for signal transmission. The compensation circuit ensures that the level shift circuit outputs the correct logic. This design is based on a 0.35µm BCD process and is simulated and verified at an operating frequency of 1MHz. The results show that the positive dv/dt immunity is greater than 350V/ns, the negative dv/dt immunity is great, the rise transmission delay is 1.494ns and the fall transmission delay is 1.345ns. Verified at different process corners and temperatures, the positive dv/dt immunity is all greater than 350V/ns. A high dv/dt immunity, low-ripple level shift circuit is realized.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Power High-Order Compensated Voltage and Current Reference Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a novel low power consumption and high accuracy bandgap voltage and current reference circuit without amplifier unit for a DC-DC Buck converter is presented. The reference voltage is derived from the bandgap topology, and the reference current is obtained by summing the proportional absolute temperature (PTAT) current and complementary absolute temperature (CTAT) current so that the temperature coefficient of the current reference can be optimized. Higher-order temperature compensation for the reference circuit is accomplished by employing two pairs of MOSFETs operating in the subthreshold region. These MOSFET pairs generate exponential compensation currents tailored for both lowtemperature and high-temperature conditions. This approach ensures the generation of a reference voltage with a minimized temperature coefficient. The circuit is designed based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18 \upmu\mathrm{m}$</tex> BCD process with a layout of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.26 ~\text{mm} \times 0.2 ~\text{mm}$</tex>. The maximum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text {REF}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{REF}}$</tex> obtained from the simulation are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1.2} \mathrm{V}$</tex> and 114.6 nA, respectively. The temperature coefficient of the reference voltage is only 1.4 ppm/°C in the range of -40 to 125°C. In the range of supply voltages of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.5 \sim 5.5 ~\mathrm{V}$</tex>, the reference voltage varies around 1.01 mV, and the line regulation is 0.028 %. And from the temperature range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex>, the variation of the reference current is only 3 nA.

articleTitle: A 12nm CMOS Rail-to-Rail Auto-Zero Operational Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on a 12nm CMOS process, a low-power, low-offset, input/output rail-to-rail auto-zero operational amplifier is proposed. The operational amplifier dynamically removes the input offset voltage by a time-interleaved auto-zero method. The rail-to-rail input common-mode voltage range and constant input transconductance of the operational amplifier are achieved by complementary differential pairs and a 1:3 current mirror. Low power consumption is achieved by a bias circuit which generates an nA-level PTAT current. Under 0.8 V supply voltage, 25°C, The operational amplifier has an input offset voltage of 2.24 µV (typical corner), an input offset current of 5 pA, an equivalent DC gain of 114.8 dB, an input transconductance variation of 5 %, and a power consumption about 3µW, and the chip area is 0.72mm * 0.99mm excluding PAD.

articleTitle: An 8.19 nW, -71.9 dBm Sensitivity, Interference-Robust Dual-Channel Wake-Up Receiver at 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A dual-channel ED-1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>(energy detector first) wake-up receiver (WuRX) with ultra-low power and high interference robustness is presented in this work. A novel dual-channel MEMS (microelectromechanical systems) matching network is adopted for filtering and providing passive voltage gain. Thanks to the high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> of film bulk acoustic resonators (FBAR) and the dual channel working framework, the rejection to amplitude modulation (AM) interference of the WuRX is greatly improved. Designed using a 65 nm CMOS process, the WuRX operates at ~2.4 GHz and features a data rate of 250 bps based on on-off keying (OOK) modulation. Post-simulation results show that the WuRX exhibits sensitivity of -71.9 dBm and power consumption of 8.19 nW from a 0.5 V supply voltage while achieving missed-detection rate (MDR) less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> and false alarm rate (FAR) less than 1/h. The WuRX achieves -39.1 dB optimal signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) to AM interference (250 bps OOK modulated interferer) near the carrier frequency, and the worst in-band SIR is -6.4 dB. At the carrier frequency of each channel, the SIR is -11.5 dB and -30.6 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A High Linearity Current-Mirror MAC Circuit Design for SRAM Computing-in-Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Computing-in-memory (CIM), as an emerging computer architecture, can reduce the power consumption and delays of data-intensive applications caused by frequent data migration. In traditional CIM architectures, high-precision convolutional computation is often performed with large computational non-linearities due to multi-bit weighting, which reduces the computational accuracy and energy efficiency of the system. This paper proposes a high linearity current-mirror MAC circuit (CMMC) and constructs a CIM architecture that can realize 8-bit MAC using a novel 8T SRAM, which adopts the current domain computation mode and has a higher computational linearity than that of the bit-line discharge mode in the charge domain. Under the 110nm process with a 1.2V supply voltage, the functional correctness of the circuit was verified through simulation, and its linearity was calculated to be up to 99.82%, significantly enhancing the accuracy of multi-bit convolutional computation. Furthermore, the storage for a single convolutional kernel in this design is unfolded in the row direction, endowing this CIM circuit architecture with excellent parallelism and scalability.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Low-Overhead SoC for Arrhythmia Detection Based on Cyclic Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease continue to pose a major threat to the lives and health of humans across the world. How to achieve portable and high-precision detection has become a research hotspot in preventing cardiovascular diseases. To address the issue of high overhead and difficulty in reconfigurable in high-precision artificial intelligence (AI) detection. This paper proposes a reconfigurable low-overhead arrhythmia detection system on chip (SoC) solution based on cyclic convolutional neural networks (CNN). The solution first involves researching the algorithms and structures of convolutional neural networks. This solution first studies the algorithms and structures of convolutional neural networks. Using cyclic CNN to classify arrhythmia, and reusing convolution and pooling modules to reduce hardware overhead. Then, by flexibly configuring the hyperparameter registers within the cyclic CNN-IP core, combined with the RISC-V instruction programming CPU method, achieved the reconfigurable CNN on SoC. Finally, in the digital backend clock gating and multi-threshold voltage techniques are adopted to reduce chip power consumption by 64.3%. In this paper, under the TSMC 65nm process the chip layout design is completed. With a supply voltage of 1V and an operating frequency of 100MHz, the classification accuracy for arrhythmias in the MIT-BIH dataset reaches 97.07%, with a chip area of 3.68 mm2 and a power consumption of 2.86 mW.

articleTitle: A Peak Current Mode Buck DC-DC Converter with Programmable Phase Shifting for Parallel Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of limited power capacity and switch stress in a single power supply, this paper designs a multi-phase interleaved parallel high-current Buck DCDC converter. The converter is based on peak current mode (PCM) to meet the power supply requirements of the equipment and reduce output voltage and current ripple. This paper proposes a programmable phase shift circuit. By setting the phase shift of the switching clock of the parallel branch converter, the power output of the converter can be easily expanded to a parallel structure of 2 to 12 phases. The circuit proposed in this paper is designed based in the SMIC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18 \upmu\mathrm{m}$</tex> 5V CMOS process for circuit and layout design. The simulation results show that when the input voltage is 5V, the output voltage is 1.5V, the switching frequency is 1 MHz, the single-phase output is 5A, and the four-phase parallel output is 20A, the output voltage ripple is 3.56 mV and 0.61 mV respectively, and the output current ripple is 11.87 mA and 8.11 mA respectively, achieving the performance of high current and low ripple output.

articleTitle: A Reactively Matched High-Power Amplifier for Ku-Band in 0.25-µm GaN Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A Ku-Band high-efficiency monolithic microwave integrated circuit high-power amplifier based on a commercially available 0.25-µm GaN technology is presented. A three-stage topology is employed in this design to enhance both gain and efficiency. The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed HPA chip, occupying an area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.1\times 3\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, features an average output power of 45.2 dBm and a peak output power of 45.6 dBm at 16.1 GHz, with a small-signal gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21} > 28\text{dB}$</tex> at 14–18 GHz. The average PAE of this power amplifier is 40.9%, with a peak PAE of 41.8% at 17.5 GHz. A flat power gain exceeding 22.7 dB is achieved with gain variation less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.5\text{dB}$</tex> across the entire bandwidth. The achieved power density is 2.69 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}/\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Multi-Level Verification Method for a Quad-Core RISC-V SoC
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Verification is a time-consuming and resource-intensive task in System-on-Chip (SoC) design. However, a single verification method often fails to effectively meet diverse verification needs. In this paper, we present a multi-level verification method that divides SoC functional verification into the module level, the connectivity layer, and the chip level. At the module level, the Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) is used to verify the function of each module. At the connectivity layer, the formal verification is employed to check connectivity and correctness. At the chip level, the coroutine co-simulation testbench (cocotb) is used to verify the overall function of the SoC. By leveraging the advantages of various verification methods at different levels, the corresponding challenges are addressed. We applied this method to verify a quad-core RISC-V SoC and achieved significant reductions in verification time.

articleTitle: In-Situ Nondestructive and Efficient Identification System for In-Plane Dimension Errors of Wafer-Level Vacuum Encapsulated MEMS Gyro
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: To monitor the MEMS process stability and pre-characterize the fabricated errors of MEMS gyro at the wafer level, an identification system is proposed that can efficiently and non-destructively characterize the beam width and the comb gap errors on the scale of hundreds of nm. Based on the static negative stiffness effect of the resonant mode of MEMS gyro, a multi-function active probe card with variable bias voltage excitation capacity and multi-parameter automatic acquisition and calculation program are designed. The proposed identification system facilitates the in situ non-destructive identification of beam width and comb gap size errors, and large data acquisition of parameters such as resistance and capacitance characteristics, resonance frequency and Q-factor characteristics, and closed-loop quadrature coupling error. The experimental results show that the etching error distributions of the drive beam widths, the sense beam widths, and the gap of the combs are −80~160 nm, −100~140 nm, and 10~310 nm. Moreover, the above dimension errors' distributions are strongly correlated with the quadrature error of MEMS gyros. The test time per die is 6 s, and the overall 6-inch wafer test time is less than 1 hour.

articleTitle: Leakage Study of Ferroelectric AlScN Capacitors Prepared on Different Bottom Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The leakage-related issues are important obstacles for advancing the ferroelectric AlScN-based electronics. Moreover, the leakage characteristics of ferroelectric AlScN films varies with different bottom electrode materials. This work explained the leakage characteristics of AlScN films prepared on different bottom electrodes (single crystal Si, Pt metal electrode) using the Poole-Frenkel emission model. Although the Pt-based AlScN capacitor realized larger remnant polarization than its Si-based counterpart, the Pt sample exhibits smaller trap energy level, leading to larger leakage current and smaller breakdown voltage. Additionally, the increased remnant polarization values of Si-based AlScN capacitor after the endurance test is explained by the decreased trap energy level and thus the increased leakage current.

Index Terms: Increase In The Number Of Cycles

articleTitle: Study on Laser Lift-Off of GaN HEMTs Grown on Fe-doped and Unintentional Doped Buffer Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Separating AlGaN/GaN HEMTs from sapphire substrates is an important segment for transferring GaN onto high thermal conductivity substrate. In this paper, using 248 nm KrF excimer laser lift-off (LLO) system, AlGaN/GaN HEMTs, grown on unintentional doped and Fe-doped buffer layer, were separated from sapphire substrates, respectively. We analyzed the changes of 2DEG characteristic, crystal characteristic and strain state of AlGaN/GaN HEMT before and after LLO by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Hall and Raman. The results indicate the structural quality of HEMT based on unintentional doped GaN buffer layer is slightly affected by LLO process. Instead, for Fe-doped GaN buffer specimen, the 2DEG characteristic has an relatively obvious degeneration after LLO, since film has generated microcracks. XRD, as well as Raman, demonstrated that the residual stress is the mayor inducement for microcracks as a result of Fe-doped GaN with higher compressive stress before LLO.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Dataflow Baseband Processor for MIMO Communication System Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technol-ogy is extensively used in various communication scenarios, posing challenges to the flexibility and real-time performance of its hardware solutions. In this paper, we propose a reconfigurable dataflow baseband processor which can flexibly deploy and efficiently execute operators extracted from MIMO communication system using dataflow graphs. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed design offers high flexibility and strong real-time performance. Additionally, it achieves 2.38×and 1.80× improvement in energy efficiency compared to similar reconfig-urable architecture and ASIC, respectively, with an antenna size of 128×8.

articleTitle: Transistor Breakdown Detection Circuit Design Based on CMOS BCD Process for High-voltage Output Stage of Neural Stimulators
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Neural stimulators with high-voltage output stage have the risk of transistor breakdown. This work presents two circuit designs for detecting malfunction of the high-voltage transistors at the output stage, so that warning signals can be generated when transistor breakdown happens. The first detection scheme uses a circuit containing a high-voltage comparator with high-voltage switches. The second scheme uses a low-voltage comparator and a step-down module to reduce the voltage of the signal to be detected. Both circuits are designed in Cadence using 180-nm BCD CMOS technology. The functions of the proposed circuits have been verified by simulation results with a high-voltage neural stimulator. Performances comparison is made and shows that scheme two could be chosen as a preferred solution. In both scenarios, the total system power consumption is below 30 μ W, and the detection response time is under 300 ns. The detection circuits proposed in this work could improve the safety of neural stimulator with high-voltage output stages.

articleTitle: A Pipelined SAR ADC with Single-Ended CDS in Fully Differential Residue Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper studies a pipelined SAR ADC with a single-ended correlated double sampling (CDS) in a fully differential residue amplifier. To improve the ADC's offset and noise performance, the single-ended CDS technique is adopted for the residue amplifier. Compared to amplifiers with double-ended CDS techniques, the amplifier with the single-ended CDS technique requires no additional settling time, avoids the risk of critical node voltages being locked, and consumes less hardware overhead. We reuse the comparator in the pipelined SAR ADC, which increases power efficiency and area utilization. The proposed design is implemented in a 65nm standard CMOS technology with a 3.3V supply voltage and 2.5V reference voltage. Extensive experiments are conducted to verify our design.

articleTitle: A 6-Bit Attenuator Design with High Attenuation Accuracy and Low Additional Phase Shift
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 6-bit attenuator is designed based on GaAs 0.15 um pHEMT process, in which different attenuation structures are cascaded in the optimal order, and inductive and capacitive phase compensation structures are added on the basis of the traditional attenuator design in order to obtain better phase shift and attenuation error, and the maximum attenuation range of 31.5 dB and the attenuation step is 0.5 dB are finally realized, and the simulation results show that the designed attenuator has the following performance. Simulation results show that the designed attenuator has an input/output return loss of less than - 19 dB, an insertion loss of less than 1.5 dB, an attenuation error of less than 0.25 dB, and an additional phase shift of ±1 in DC-4 GHz, and meanwhile, the area of the designed chip is 1.8×0.9×0.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of Medical Privacy Protection Circuit Based on Cross Obfuscation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the rise of the Internet of Things, smart healthcare with remote monitoring and diagnosis enables patients to reduce the number and duration of hospitalizations, thereby reducing the pressure on doctors. However, the transmission data of disease detection chips is susceptible to cache attacks, leading to user health data leakage. Hardware level encryption design has become a research hotspot. Firstly, by adding a Mask channel at the upper level of each convolution layer, the preprocessed data is transmitted simultaneously with the obfuscated data, and the channel exchange during transmission is utilized to protect user privacy; Secondly, there is a redundancy mechanism between the input matrix and weight matrix of the storage module, and invalid values are added to the redundant parts to prevent cache attacks from stealing user information; Finally, add multi temporal obfuscation to the first input data to achieve the different lengths between the first and subsequent data. The protection circuit designed in this article achieves user privacy protection on the basis of only increasing hardware overhead by 2.5%, power consumption overhead by 3.61%, and not affecting disease monitoring accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Additional Doping in Source/Drain Extension Region towards OFF-state Current Suppression in GAA-NSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Gate-all-around field effect transistor (GAAFET) provides excellent gate controllability, which effectively suppresses short-channel effect (SCE). Therefore, GAAFET makes it highly promising for sub-3nm node. However, the OFF-state current resulted from the dramatically change of doping concentration at the boundaries between source/drain extension region and channel region is still a critical challenge to be solved. In this study, a novel approach involving additional doping in source/drain extension region (ADER) is proposed to suppress OFF-state leakage current, and a comparative analysis among junctionless GAAFET (JLFET) and junctionless accumulation mode GAAFET (JAMFET) is conducted. Notably, the proposed device structure avoids introducing any extra lithography process. Furthermore, the impact of structural parameters on OFF-state and ON-state current of above is investigated. In conclusion, this research presents an effective method of p-type doping in extension region to enhance device performances without significantly increasing process complexity and costs.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarization Multi-Mode Multi-Drop Dielectric Waveguide Channel for Sub-Terahertz High-Capacity Interconnect
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarization multi-mode multi-drop silicon dielectric waveguide channel for sub-terahertz interconnect, which utilizes both polarization-division multiplexing and mode-division multiplexing techniques to expand the channel capacity. The waveguide channel transmits four modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{K}},\ \mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{y}},\ \mathrm{E}_{21}^{\mathrm{K}},\ \mathrm{E}_{21}^{\mathrm{y}})$</tex> with two orthogonal polarizations on a single bus waveguide. The system consists of five mode couplers for mode conversions, i.e., the quasi-transverse electromagnetic mode from metallic microstrip lines to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{y}}$</tex> mode, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{y}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{y}}$</tex> mode, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{y}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{21}^{\mathrm{y}}$</tex> mode, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{21}^{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> mode. Numerical simulation results show that the optimal coupling losses for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{x}}, \mathrm{E}_{11}^{\mathrm{y}}, \mathrm{E}_{21}^{\mathrm{x}}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{21}^{\mathrm{y}}$</tex> modes are 3.7 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}, 4.8\text{dB}, 5.7\text{dB}$</tex>, and 3.1 dB, respectively. The respective 3-dB bandwidths are 137–170 GHz, 146–176 GHz, 140–170 GHz, and 142–183 GHz, with mode crosstalk lower than -19 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}, -15\text{dB}, -19\text{dB}$</tex>, and -15 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Research of Key Technologies for 12-bit SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the rapid development of modern intelligent industries such as wireless communication, the Internet of Things, medical devices, and autonomous driving technology, the performance requirements for smart sensors are increasingly high for analog-to-digital converters. This article conducts a survey of a large number of SAR ADCs, summarizes the design methods of various key circuit modules, and designs a 12-bit, 25MS/s sampling rate fully differential input SAR ADC. This paper presents a 12-bit 25MS/s successive approximation register analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC) based on the extended C-2C capacitor array and FIA comparator, the structure not only speeds up the level conversion rate, reduces power consumption, but also reduces the mismatch of the bridging capacitor. The SAR ADC is realized in a 55nm CMOS process. In the supply voltage 1.2V, sampling rate 25MS/s, input signal frequency close to the Nyquist frequency, the SAR ADC pre-simulation results show that its ENOB is 11.89bits, SNDR is 73.34dB, SFDR is 83.42dBc. Post-simulation results show that the ENOB of SAR ADC is 10.73bits, SNDR is 73.34dB, SFDR is 83.42dBc, SNDR is 66.36dB, SFDR is 82.16dBc, power consumption is 417.59µW, FoMW is 9.83fJ/conv-step, FoMS is 171.12dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Compensation Circuit for Enhanced Linearity and Accuracy in In-Memory Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In-memory computing (IMC) based on non-volatile memory faces several challenges, such as IR Drop effects and inter-channel gain errors caused by non-ideal factors in the IMC's readout system. This paper proposes a novel compensation circuit incorporating differential port clamping and offset storage to address these issues. The designed circuit ensures consistent and linear device output current. In a 55-nm CMOS process, PVT and Monte Carlo simulation results demonstrate a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$96 \%$</tex> reduction in current non-linearity within a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0-40 \upmu ~\mathrm{A}$</tex> range of device output current and a 99.9 % reduction in inter-channel gain error (3б), indicating significant improvement over conventional methods.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Hardware Circuit for Elliptic Curve Cryptographic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
