abstract: Accompanied by the development of computer technology, cryptography has become a key technology to ensure information security. Elliptic curve cryptographic algorithm has been the key research object of cryptographers in recent years, and SM2 algorithm, as a cryptographic algorithm independently developed by China, has great advantages in algorithmic performance and other aspects. Based on SM2 algorithm, this paper realizes the hardware design of four functions: decryption, encryption, digital signature verification and digital signature. The scalar multiplication module is the core module in SM2 algorithm, and the performance of scalar multiplication module determines the performance of SM2 algorithm. In this paper, we first analyze and design the NAF -based scalar multiplication module, which reduces the number of point addition operations and thus shortens the operation time of the scalar multiplication module, and then process the point doubling and point addition modules called by scalar multiplication, and then design the parallel point doubling and point addition operation circuits based on the Jacobian projective coordinate system, which shortens the operation time of the point doubling and point addition modules, after deeply investigating the data flow in the Jacobian projective coordinate system. Finally, we also design parallel modulo multiplication circuits to shorten the computation time of the modulo multiplication module. The main contribution of this paper in improving the performance of the scalar multiplication module is the simultaneous optimization of the elliptic curve arithmetic layer and the modulo multiplication arithmetic layer, which greatly reduces the computation time of the scalar multiplication module, and is verified on the Xilinx Virtex-7, and the experimental results show that the speed of the optimized scalar multiplication module has been significantly improved.

articleTitle: Statistical Prediction-Based Traffic Model for Radiation Sensor Networks by Multi-Resolution Analysis and Machine Learning Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In conventional network traffic models, packets duration time is described by a heavy-tailed function. However, heavy-tailed functions cannot precisely reflect the characteristic of transmitting rate during an active period in wireless time-variant channel in sensor networks. To obtain a more comprehensive description, we propose a statistical prediction-based (SP) traffic model using Maximal Overlap Discrete Wavelet Transform (MODWT) to make multiresolution analysis of the channel property and Support Vector Machine (SVM) to dynamically capture the instantaneous variation. A learning method is also derived for adapting the accuracy of prediction. Furthermore, an analytical expression is proposed to calculate the aggregate network traffic flow. The simulation results show that the fit of reality is improved by the proposed model.

articleTitle: X-Band GaN Internal Matching Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 9–11 GHz power amplifier based on high pressure gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) is designed. The matching network uses a modified version of the power separator structure, which enables a wider bandwidth at the same size. This power amplifier uses a chip with a gate size of 0.25um, which has a greater gain compared with a chip with a gate size of 0.45um. The simulation results show that in the 9–11 GHz frequency band, the power amplifier performs the saturation output power is more than 54 dBm, the gain is greater than 9 dB, the power additional efficiency is higher than 45%, and the input echo loss S11 is less than-10dB. The total size of this power amplifier is 26.4mm×17.4mm × 4.6mm, with miniaturization and high integration characteristics.

articleTitle: An 8×8-Pixel LiDAR Receiver with Multi-Echo Recording TDC for Background Light Interference Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper reports a light detection and range (LiDAR) receiver based on an 8 × 8 Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) array. A Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) capable of performing photon coincidence detection and recording multiecho is proposed to filter out background noise interference and improve the signal-to-noise ratio. The experimental results show that the active region of the 8×8 SPAD receiver array can be reconfigurable to suit the optic focal point, thereby avoiding the influence of SPADs outside the optic focal point.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band LNA Base on 65nm CMOS for Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Baseed on 65nm CMOS process, a low noise amplifier(LNA) was designede for Ka-band. By studying the influence of transistor size and bias voltage on noise figure and gain performance, the transistor size and bias voltage under low noise and high gain condition are determined. The transformer matching network is adopted for the input, output and inter-stage matching of LNA, which reduces the LNA size to 0.75 mm × 0.52mm and improves the circuit isolation. The test results show that the maximum in-band gain of the LNA is 18 dB, the minimum noise figure is 5 dB at 1 V supply voltage In the RF transmitter and receiver system, this LNA has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Review of TSVs Testing Between Chiplets
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As semiconductor technology advances, traditional 2D integrated circuits can no longer meet demands, leading to the rise of Chiplet heterogeneous integration. Through-Silicon Via (TSV) technology enhances data transfer speed, bandwidth, and integration density while reducing power consumption and package size through vertical interconnections. This paper introduces pre-bond and post-bond TSV testing methods, including on-chip and probe-based techniques, and highlights the TSV Built-In Self-Test (BIST) repair mechanism for identifying and repairing defects. These advancements address TSV testing complexity challenges, providing insights for optimizing 3D stacked integrated circuits.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise Energy-Efficient Double-Tail Dynamic Latch Comparator
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As the primary source of power consumption and noise in ADCs, the comparator's performance is critical to the ADC performance. This paper proposes a low-noise energy-efficient double-tail dynamic latch comparator. By analyzing the traditional double-tail dynamic latch comparator structure and its noise source, this work proposes improvements that balance noise and power consumption. The pre-amplification stage is enhanced with cross-coupled pairs to boost amplification gain, the latch stage current transistors are switched to NMOS for lower power consumption, and capacitors are added to the first-stage output to minimize equivalent input noise. The prototype is designed in UMC 110nm process, and the layout area of the proposed comparator is 8 µm × 70.4 µm. At a power supply voltage of 3.3V, operating frequency of 40MHz, and a comparison step size of 244µ V, the comparator achieves an input noise of 207 µ Vrms and a FoM of 8.3349 nJ·(µV)2.

articleTitle: A Wide Input Range LDO with Floating Ground Output
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, for the problem of unstable ground and wide input voltage range in automotive electronic system, a wide input range LDO with floating ground output based on 0.5um SOI process is proposed. Unlike the traditional LDO, the power transistor of this design adopts the high-voltage NMOS, and the output is adjusted through voltage sampling and the negative feedback loop. The design achieves constant voltage output relative to the power supply and widens the input voltage range. Simulation results show that the input voltage range of the designed LDO can reach 5.5-65V. The line regulation can reach 0.004mV/V and PSRR at 100Hz is 81.6dB.

articleTitle: A 8bit, 2.5 ps Resoultion Time-to-Digital Converter in 130nm SiGe Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 8hit, 2.5ps two-step time-to-digital converter is implemented in 130 nm SiGe technology, with a matching coarse-fine gating circuit to reduce transmission error. A low-precision delay chain quantization architecture is used for the coarse stage to achieve wide dynamic range. And a high-precision structure based on time amplifier and unit time comparator is used for the fine stage to ensure higher resolution. Compared with traditional Vernier and exponential structure, this structure balances inter stage matching and linearity. The simulation results show that the time-to-digital converter can balance the performance of resolution, linearity and dynamic range. DNL and INL are, respectively, 0.86 LSB and 1.019 LSB. It can be used as a phase detector with digital output.

articleTitle: A Digital Low Drop Out (DLDO) Regulators with Transient Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on the DLDO structure employing a coarse-fine dual-loop design, this paper proposes a transient-enhanced auxiliary loop. The transient-enhanced auxiliary loop leverages the fast response capability of flip-flop circuits to achieve rapid transient response. The DLDO regulator is implemented using a 55nm CMOS process, with a load capacitance of 400pF. Under typical process conditions and room temperature simulation, the static current measures 7.15µA. The reference voltage is set at 0.7V, with a maximum load current of 20mA and a minimum of 4mA. During load transitions from 4mA to 20mA, the switching time is 30ns, resulting in a downshoot voltage of 62.78mV and a recovery time of 0.55µs. Conversely, when transitioning from 20mA to 4mA, the switching time remains 30ns, with an overshoot voltage of 81.3mV and a recovery time of 0.74µs. The current efficiency, as depicted in the figures, reaches 99.9%.

articleTitle: Hardware Design and Security Analysis for cSHAKE256 in PQC SIAKE
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the development of quantum computing, traditional public-key encryption algorithms are facing unprecedented threats, and it is urgent to develop cryptographic algorithms that can resist the attack from quantum computing. SIAKE is a Supersingular Isogeny based authenticated key exchange algorithm. In SIAKE, cSHAKE256 is a key step in 2-Key PKE based on homology calculations. cSHAKE256 is an extensible hash function in the SHA-3 family that further enhances flexibility and security with Customization strings and function names. This paper presents a hardware structure of cSHAKE256 suitable for SIAKE. First, the domain separation module specific to cSHAKE256 is designed. Secondly, the iteration function is optimized to achieve 2 iterations in one cycle. Finally, the 3-stage pipeline structure is adopted in Keccak function algorithm and the wheel constant is simplified, which can greatly improve the throughput and save some resources. The design is verified on FPGA Xilinx Virtex-7, the results show that the designed cSHAKE256 hardware unit has a maximum operating frequency of 217MHz. Finally, the hardware structure of cSHAKE256 is analyzed for side channel security. The design and implementation of cSHAKE256 is proven to be directly applicable to SIAKE, providing it with the necessary security and randomness.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Different Verification Platforms of AHB-SPI
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper uses an Advanced High-performance Bus - Serial Peripheral Interface (AHB-SPI) module as the verification target and compares three verification platforms: Universal Verification Methodology/SystemVerilog (UVM/SV), the COroutine based COsimulation TestBench (cocotb), and UVM-Python. UVM/SV, the widely adopted method in the industry, offers a robust framework with modular and reusable components. However, it is constrained by its inherent nature as a hardware description language and deep learning curve of SV. Cocotb, based on Python, separates the simulation from the verification, mitigating some limitations associated with hardware description languages. Nevertheless, it lacks standardization and reusability, making it difficult to achieve uniformity. UVM-Python integrates the strengths of both approaches, offering a standardized yet flexible verification methodology. The study seeks to enhance the understanding of different verification platforms and provide guidance for verification engineers in selecting the most suitable methods for their projects.

articleTitle: A 48 V/1 MHz Monolithic GaN DC-DC Buck Converter with Sub-20-ns Dead-Time Control
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Fixed dead-time controlling strategy is widely adopted in conventional converter design, while it suffers from the potential issue of simultaneous conduction under different loading conditions. This work aims to adaptively optimize the dead-time at the monolithic integration level through simulation software, Advanced Design System (ADS). In a 48 V GaN buck converter, the sub-20-ns adaptive low-side dead-time control and high-side dead-time control are achieved at 1 MHz operation frequency. The proposed dead-time control circuit exhibits a maximum efficiency up to 91.4 %, facilitated by the adaptive and self-generated dead-time design.

articleTitle: A High-Order Temperature Compensation Bandgap Voltage Reference with Line Sensitivity Enhanced
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposed a bandgap voltage reference with high-order temperature compensation structure, line sensitivity enhancement structure, and zero power start-up circuit. The circuit is designed using SMIC 0.18-µm BCD process, with a working temperature range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\sim 125^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, a stable reference voltage of 735mV, and normal operation within the VDD range of 3.7V-4.7V. Adopting a simple line sensitivity enhancement structure to improve the accuracy of the current source mirror and the overall line sensitivity of the system. When VDD is 4.4V, the temperature coefficient of proposed bandgap voltage reference is simulated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.090\text{ppm}/^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, and the line sensitivity is 1.20%/V.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based PCB Routing Using Dueling Double Deep Q Network
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the development of technology, the circuits on printed circuit boards(PCB) become more and more complex. Traditional PCB routing methods often rely on experiences and heuristic rules, which are inefficient and difficult to guarantee the global optimal solution in complex design. This paper introduces a multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm based on local observation, which is designed to optimize the auto routing process of PCB by dueling double deep Q network(D3QN). This method combines the advantages of deep reinforcement learning and double Q learning, and can learn and optimize strategies more effectively in high-dimensional state space. The experimental results show that the routing method in this paper shows high adaptability and flexibility in dealing with routing tasks, which not only improves the routing efficiency, but also improves the routing rate.

articleTitle: A Broadband Compact mm-Wave Series Doherty Power Amplifier Using Coupler Balun-Based Active Load Modulation Network in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband, compact mm-Wave series Doherty power amplifier utilizing a coupler balun-based active load modulation network in 65-nm CMOS technology. The coupler-based baluns in the PA output network facilitate power combining, impedance matching, differential to single-ended conversion, and active load modulation. Adaptive biasing circuit further enhances the main/auxiliary PA cooperation. The proposed PA exhibits wideband PBO efficiency enhancement over a frequency range of 24 GHz to 36 GHz, achieving a fractional bandwidth of 40%. At the operating frequency of 29 GHz, the PA achieves a saturated power of 24.3 dBm and 32.4% peak PAE. At 7.5 dB PBO, the simulated PAE is 24.5%, demonstrating 1.68× efficiency enhancement compared to an ideal class-B PA with the same peak PAE at OP1dB.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Bandwidth and Low-Distortion Two-Stage Cascode Amplifier Based on 22-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced operational amplifier design, which achieves a significant bandwidth expansion of approximately 15% through an innovative application of the gm/Id methodology. The design refines the traditional folded casco de structure, integrating a modified input stage with a symmetrical PMOS input transistor to reduce circuit mismatch. Employing TSMC's 18rf process library, the design and simulation were executed within the Cadence platform. The resulting operational amplifier is capable of operating over a wide temperature range from −25°C to 125°C, consistently delivering an open-loop gain exceeding 80 dB, a phase margin beyond 60 degrees, a unit gain bandwidth over 80 MHz, a common mode rejection ratio above 60 dB, a power supply rejection ratio in excess of 80 dB, and an output voltage swing that closely approaches the positive and negative supply rails.

articleTitle: A Speed and Accuracy Enhanced Current Sensor for Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A fast-response and high-accuracy novel current sensor applied for converter is presented in this paper. Dynamic bias feedback technology is applied in the amplifier to improve the speed and stability of the current sensor under a wide range of load currents. A shunt circuit and a current compensation circuit are implemented to enhance sensing accuracy. The proposed current sensor is designed based on a standard 0.15-µm CMOS process. The simulation results show that the proposed current sensor offers fast responsiveness with a response time under 22 ns. With load current ranging from 100mA-2A, the current sensing accuracy can achieve 99.77%.

articleTitle: Thermal Reliability Simulation Analysis of Planar Microsystem
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As a typical representative technological route of chip technology, microsystems have gradually become one of the main solutions for the small-volume, speciality applications. Heat is the main limitation of the microsystem in speciality applications. This paper takes the planar microsystem as the research object, a finite element simulation is established by ANSYS to evaluate the maximum temperature of the different dies under different heat source distribution. The simulation results are of great significance for the high-reliability design and applications of planar microsystems.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a High-Performance DSP External Memory Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: To meet the need for rapid data transmission between the core of high-performance Digital Signal Processor (DSP) chips and external memory, as well as to manage different types of external memory flexibly, we have designed an External Memory Controller (EMC). This module not only manages multiple peripherals and supports concurrent and parallel access but also provides excellent flexibility and configurability, making it suitable for various system requirements. The EMC includes SDMA, IDMAO, IDMA1, and a dedicated ET debugging DMA channel. The SDMA channel facilitates data transfer between multiple peripherals connected to the DMA Switch Fabric outside the core and the core's internal memory spaces. The IDMA channels support fast data transfer between any two memory locations within the core. The ET dedicated DMA channel is used for JTAG debugging, ensuring the correct operation, superior performance, and reliability of the DSP chip. The EMC operates independently of CPU control, enabling rapid and large-scale data movement. After functional simulation verification and coverage analysis, the designed EMC component has achieved the expected objectives and meets the design requirements.

articleTitle: An Airflow Volumetric Flowmeter Using ScAlN-Based Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers (PMUTs) in Small-Diameter Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an airflow volumetric flowmeter utilizing ScAIN-based piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) for application in small-diameter pipelines. The device contains two pieces of 4×4 PMUTs arrays with resonant frequency of 171 kHz. The dimension of the PMUTs array is about 4×4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, allowing it to measure gas flow in a pipeline with an inner diameter of 6 mm. By applying voltage excitation, the downstream and upstream waveform signals from PMUTs are processed through cross-correlation and interpolation to determine the time difference of ultrasonic wave propagation in the gas. The flowmeter maintains a relative error within 3% across a reference volumetric flow range of 2–800 L/H. The results indicate potential application of PMUTs for accurately measuring gas flow in small-diameter pipelines.

articleTitle: Measurement-Driven Automated Design of High-Efficiency Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In modern power amplifier (PA) design, model-based approaches combining EDA tools are commonly employed. To avoid numerous iterations due to inaccuracies of transistor models and achieve first-design-pass goal, this paper proposes a measurement-driven automated PA design approach utilizing load-pull measurement data and machine learning methods for the design of harmonic controlled PA. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a PA operating at 2.4 GHz was designed and measured with a maximum power-added efficiency (PAE) of 73.4% and a maximum output power of 40 dBm.

articleTitle: A Bandgap Reference with High Power Supply Rejection Ratio at Low Supply Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The bandgap reference is a widely used module in integrated circuits. The main function of this circuit is to provide reference voltage or current independent of temperature, supply voltage and process. In this paper, a bandgap reference module is designed based on 130nm process that can operate at lower voltage sources with high power supply rejection ration. The power supply noise is resisted by generating a localized voltage. Simulation results show that the power supply rejection ratio can reach 91.4dB at typical process corner. Over the temperature range of -40°C to 125°C, the temperature coefficient of reference output voltage is 24.27PPM/°C. In addition, this design uses an inverter-based start-up circuit, which makes the bandgap reference source have good stability and reliability.

articleTitle: Blurred Image Restoration CMOS Image Sensor Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In conventional Time Delayed Integration(TDI) image sensors, the sensor is prone to vibration due to interference, which makes the exposure information of each row of pixels unsynchronized, thus leading to image distortion and blurring. In order to solve the image blurring problem, this paper proposes an analog-domain blurred image restoration(BIR) algorithm by investigating the working principle of the TDI CMOS image sensor (CIS) and why sensor vibration leads to image blurring. Then, the algorithm is modeled in MATLAB and the feasibility of the algorithm is verified. After that, the circuit structure of the algorithm implementation was designed according to the principle of the algorithm. Finally, the circuit simulation required for the BIR algorithm is completed using the 0.11µm CMOS process.

articleTitle: Multi-Head Attention Hardware Implementation and Side-Channel Security Analysis for Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative hardware implementation of the complete multi-head attention mechanism, reducing resource consumption and boosting speed while addressing the Transformer model's computational complexity. Experimental results show that the total utilization of logic lookup tables (LUT) is 28,218, accounting for 60% of the total resources, while registers (regs) used are 16,648, accounting for 16% of the total resources. The model with a dimension of 48 was verified on an FPGA development board with the model number xc7k160tfbg676-1. The data of the model was quantized to 16-bit fixed-point, and the final results showed an average error of 0.0069 compared to the software calculations. The execution time was 1.3871 ms, which is 30.26% faster than the 1.9891 ms required by the software. Additionally, by reproducing the typical systolic array structure in matrix operations and implementing side-channel attacks based on its power consumption characteristics, the model structure and parameters were inferred using simple power analysis (SPA) methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing IMU Navigation Systems with LSTM and ZUPT: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a cutting-edge approach to eliminating errors in Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) systems and enhancing trajectory positioning using machine learning techniques. By remotely acquiring IMU data through a Raspberry Pi, the system utilizes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to reduce errors. It then employs Zero Velocity Update (ZUPT) to estimate speed and plot trajectories. Our methodology achieves significant reductions in IMU error, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) below 0.08, and maintains a positioning accuracy around 2%. The results demonstrate the efficacy of neural network learning in precise trajectory tracking and positioning, highlighting the transformative potential of machine learning in IMU-based navigation technologies.

articleTitle: A Self-Biased Triggered DDSCR Device for Low Supply Voltage Amplifier ASICs ESD Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A direct bidirectional current discharge path between the input/output (I/O) and ground (GND) is essential for robust protection of charging device models (CDM) in the tightly constrained design parameters of advanced low-voltage (LV) processes. The Dual Direction Silicon Controlled Rectifier (DDSCR) serves as an ESD protection device with high efficiency unit area discharge, enabling bidirectional electrostatic protection. However, the high trigger voltage of conventional DDSCR makes it unsuitable for ASICs used for preamplification of biomedical signals, which only operate at low supply voltage. To address this issue, a Self-biased Triggered DDSCR(STDDSCR) structure is proposed to further reduce the trigger voltage. When the ESD pulse comes, the external RC trigger circuit controls the PMOS turn-on by self-bias, and the current release path is opened in advance to reduce the trigger voltage. As the ESD pulse voltage increases, the SCR loop opens to establish positive feedback and drain the amplified current. Additionally, the junction capacitance is decreased through high-resistance epitaxy and low-concentration P-well injection to further lower the trigger voltage. The simulation results of LTspice and TCAD respectively demonstrate that ESD devices can clamp transient high voltages earlier, with low parasitic capacitance and leakage current suitable for ESD protection of high-speed ports up to 1.5V under normal operating conditions.

articleTitle: A Scalable Model for On-Chip Interdigital Capacitor Based on Space-Mapping Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A scalable model for on-chip interdigital capacitor is proposed based on space-mapping neural network (SMNN), which combines the equivalent circuit of capacitor and perceptron neural network. By expanding the traditional series equivalent circuit into a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex>-type structure and adding a series network of resistor and capacitor to characterize the coupling effect, the variation of the equivalent series resistance (ESR) and S-parameter with frequency can be effectively predicted. According to the mathematical equation, the value of each component for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\text{-}\pi$</tex> equivalent circuit model can be quickly and correctly obtained. In order to effectively improve the prediction accuracy and convergence speed of neural network, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Levenberg-Marquardt Back Propagation (LMBP) are used to select and optimize the weights and thresholds of the neural networks. Compared with the traditional neural network model, the proposed SMNN reduces the number of neurons required to map the input-output nonlinear relationship, so that the modeling time is only reduced to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10 \sim 15$</tex> seconds, and the test data accuracy is good.

articleTitle: A Low-Power ADC for CIM with Non-Linear Quantisation, Max Pooling, and Configurable-Threshold ReLU
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: For energy-efficient compute-in-memory (CIM) macros, peripheral circuits such as analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) consume the majority of power. Traditional ADCs often struggle to balance performance and power consumption effectively. This paper proposes a novel low-power ADC specifically designed for CIM applications, which integrates a configurable-threshold rectified linear unit (ReLU) function and max pooling function. Compared to the traditional ADC, the proposed ADC reduces conversions by over 80% without additional analog circuitry. Furthermore, the proposed ADC optimizes the quantization curve with an average switching power consumption of 37.8 CVref2 while maintaining network recognition accuracy. The proposed ADC is simulated using a 55-nm CMOS process with a supply voltage of 1.2 V. At a sampling frequency of 2 MHz and across the full input range, the analog power consumption is 1.6 µW. Through ADC modeling and algorithmic simulations, the classification of the CIFAR-10 dataset using the VGG16 network achieved an accuracy of 92.87%.

articleTitle: Quantitative Study of DNA Probe Density for Enhanced Biosensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to explore a biosensing method based on DNA probe quantification and its applications. A single-stranded DNA probe sequence was selected and immobilized on the surface of a screen-printed electrode through Au-S self-assembly. The experimental conditions including probe concentration, incubation time, and detection time were initially optimized. Differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) was employed to study the binding efficiency of the target sequence. Subsequently, chronocoulometry (CC) was used to investigate the probe density after incubating the probe sequence on the electrode. The CC results together with the corresponding DPV response signals showed that the highest hybridization efficiency of 22-mer DNA probe was obtained when the probe density reached 5.57×l0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> molecule/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. In addition, it was found that the electrostatic repulsion force caused by the high-density probe was higher than that of the low-density probe on the detection signal. The proposed hypothesis was further verified by applying this quantitative method to determine the hybridization efficiency using a long DNA probe (73-mer) and a short one (20-mer). This study provides an important theoretical and experimental basis for the development of advanced biosensing methods.

articleTitle: A Five-Stage Pipelined Processor Circuit Design Based on RISC-V
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the field of processor design, RISC-V instruction set has the advantages of modularity, low power consumption, high performance and easy scalability. Five-level pipelining has significant advantages in improving processor utilization and resolving performance bottlenecks. This paper presents the design principle, implementation method and performance evaluation of a five-stage pipeline processor based on RISC-V. The pipelined processor circuit implements the overlapping execution of instructions by adding pipelined registers between each subprocess, holding all the information that the previous stage wants to pass to the next stage. Improve instruction throughput, shorten program execution time, improve processor performance, realize the simulation verification of single instruction.

articleTitle: A High Voltage Driver Amplifier with Wide Output Swing, High Linearity, High Output Accuracy and Compact Size
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a high voltage driver amplifier with compact die size and high output accuracy. The amplifier utilizes two stage fully differential architecture to achieve high voltage gain, ensuring that the relative error of the output voltage is less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\%$</tex>. It operates with three power supplies: 3.3V, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 17\mathrm{V}$</tex>, and adopts various simulating for power-up protection to enhance practical reliability. To optimize chip area, a combination of high voltage and low voltage MOS transistors is employed. The circuit is fabricated using the 180nm BCD process, with a chip area of 0.98mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The testing results show that when driving a load of 13pF in parallel with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$143.4\mathrm{k}\Omega$</tex>, it can achieve output voltage swing of greater than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 13.2\mathrm{V}$</tex>, with output relative error less than 5%.

Author Keywords: mixed high voltage and low voltage MOS transistors

articleTitle: Design of HD Real-time Video Defogging System Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The research in this paper focuses on three main aspects: Improving the dark channel prior defogging algorithm to make it suitable for implementation on FPGA; Designing a high-definition real-time video defogging system capable of supporting a resolution of 1920×1080 and a frame rate of 60 frames per second; Comparing the defogging results of different algorithms qualitatively and quantitatively. This paper optimizes the dark channel prior defogging algorithm by separately calculating the transmission rate for the sky region based on the high grayscale values in the dark channel image, aiming to reduce color deviation in the sky region after defogging. The proposed defogging algorithm demonstrates efficient performance on FPGA, producing vivid and clear defogged videos while maintaining real-time processing capability. This enhancement effectively improves the usability of video equipment in foggy weather conditions.

articleTitle: Detection of Electronic Component Anomalies Through Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In modern electronics systems, predicting and preventing failures and malfunctions is crucial for ensuring reliability and reducing downtime. In this study, we present an approach for predicting electronics failure and malfunction by analyzing temperature and vibration data collected under various operational conditions. Our approach integrates data from multiple sensors monitoring temperature and vibration levels, providing a comprehensive view of system health. After setting the sensors, several data under different conditions were obtained. Through extensive experimentation and validation on real-world datasets, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our vibration and temperature data in anticipating electronics failures and malfunctions. Furthermore, we discuss the practical implications of our research, including potential applications for condition-based maintenance and proactive fault management in electronics systems. Overall, this work contributes to enhancing the reliability and performance of electronics systems in various applications, ranging from consumer electronics to industrial automation.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise Weak Current Detection Amplifier for Wide Temperature Ranges
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A low-noise weak current detection amplifier is proposed, featuring a transimpedance amplifier (TIA) with adjustable pseudo-resistance to provide high transimpedance gain. The amplifier's input is equipped with low-leakage electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection to achieve ultra-low input leakage, effectively addressing the leakage issues present in traditional ESD circuits. This paper meticulously analyzes the impact of integrating low-leakage ESD circuits on the stability and noise performance of the TIA system, and proposes viable solutions. Notably, the noise is effectively suppressed even at elevated temperatures. The prototype amplifier demonstrates an RMS integrated noise of 3.05 fA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf> within the circuit bandwidth, operating at a transimpedance gain of 100G and a temperature of 85°C.

articleTitle: Software-Defined Radio Technology Drives the Development of RF Microsystem
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The traditional RF front-end is based on compound semiconductor devices with a large number of discrete devices. RF microsystem is the miniaturization of RF front-end by two-dimensional integration, with low integration density and large size. In this work, we design a new RF microsystem based on the software-defined radio (SDR) architecture, using RF transceiver SoC and FPGA. Compared with traditional RF microsystem, more than 20 discrete devices are reduced, with a 95% reduction in size by three-dimensional heterogeneous integration.

articleTitle: A New Fault Location Technique for Coaxial Cable Using Impedance Spectroscopies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel fault location technique based on impedance spectroscopies. Assisted by COMSOL Multiphysics, cables with and without insulation degradation are modeled efficiently and their broadband impedance spectroscopies and propagation constant that vary with the sweeping frequency are computed. Then by applying a suitable integral transform to the input impedance spectroscopies, the faults in a degraded cable can be detected and located precisely. Simulation results show that failure sections can be located with high accuracy even if the cable length is as long as 500m, illustrating that this method can be applied in modeling failure cable for fault diagnosis and analysis.

articleTitle: A 16-bit Low-Power DAC Based on Hybrid Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The design of high-precision digital-to-analog converter (DAC) is crucial for applications requiring accurate signal conversion in various high-performance systems. This paper presents the design of a high-precision DAC circuit with a 16-bit resolution, based on a hybrid structure. The structure uses a “2+6+8” segmented thermometer code, incorporating both a voltage-type R-2R ladder and a current injection structure. The 8-bit LSB control the position of the current sources connected to the resistor string, generating different weighted voltages through resistor division. Additionally, a high-gain, wide-output swing operational amplifier buffer is designed to amplify the output voltage while maintaining low current consumption. This design is able to derive high resolution and high performance, in terms of differential nonlinearity (DNL) and integral nonlinearity (INL), and less power consumption comparing with conventional DACs. Simulation results validate clearly the effectiveness of this design. At a sampling frequency of 200 kHz, the output signal's signal-to-noise and distortion ratio (SNDR) is 91.1 dB, and spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) is 105.43 dB. And the total average power consumption is only 6.3 mW.

articleTitle: A 350MHz, 10bit, 500-fs Resolution Asynchronous Pipelined-SAR Time-to-Digital Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: High-speed, high-resolution and high-linearity time-to-digital converters (TDCs) are the key components in digital phase-locked-loops(DPLLs) and time-domain analog-to-digital converters(ADCs). The time amplifier (TA) based TDCs have achieved high resolution. However, the variation of the TA gain reduces linearity, which need additional calibration circuits. This paper proposes a high-resolution and high-speed asynchronous pipelined-successive approximation register(SAR) time-to-digital converter (TDC). The one-bit delay stage of the proposed TDC is realized by a constant slope digital-to-time converter (DTC) which achieves high linearity and high resolution. To improve the conversion rate of the SAR TDC, an asynchronous pipelined operation strategy is proposed. Moreover, a pulse width recovery circuit is proposed to maintain the linearity of the DTC at a high conversion rate. Simulations show that the TDC designed in 40 nm CMOS achieves 10-bit, 500 fs of time resolution, 0.8 LSB DNL and 1.6 LSB INL at 350 MHz sampling frequency consuming 14.72 mW power, which corresponds to 106.74 fJ/Conv. FoM.

articleTitle: Advanced Design and Optimization of CNTFET-Based SRAM Circuits Using a 180nm Process Design Ki
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) is a critical component in modern micro-architectures, playing a pivotal role in Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs) and Systems on Chip (SoCs). This paper presents a novel SRAM design based on Carbon Nanotube Field-Effect Transistors (CNTFETs), used a 180nm Process Design Kit (PDK). A comprehensive PDK for 180nm CNTFETs has been developed, encompassing Parameterized Cells (Pcells), compact models, Design Rule Checking (DRC)/Layout Versus Schematic (LVS)/Parasitic Extraction (PEX) rules, and standard cell libraries, all of which are compatible with industry-standard Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. This work provides an important reference for the development of next-generation SRAM and other circuits utilizing CNTFET technology.

articleTitle: Design of K-Band Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) Based on Active-Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper designs a two-stage cascade low noise amplifier (LNA) based on a FET (NE3517S03) and innovatively develops a common-base PNP microstrip stub structure as an active-bias circuit. The active-bias LNA's simulation results are compared with the passive-bias LNA's, which show that the designed active-bias LNA has 35.17 dB power gain, and 1.12 dB noise figure (NF) with better performance at 23.9GHz to 24.1 GHz. According, the LNA has lower noise and the largest gain when compared to published K-Band LNAs based on the FET. This proposed LNA is effective for K-band anti-collision radar in automobiles.

articleTitle: An 18.6-to-27.6GHz High-Linear Wideband Low-Noise Amplifier Based on Gate-Source and Gate-Drain Magnetically Coupled Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-linearity wideband low noise amplifier (LNA) for 18.6-to-27.6GHz mm-Wave communications. It features gate-source and gate-drain magnetically coupled resonators (MCRs) at the first and second stage, respectively, improving both bandwidth and noise figure (NF). The gate-source feedback MCR at the first stage together with shunt LC network achieve wideband input-impedance matching and optimize NF, while the gate-drain MCR and the capacitive feedback at the second stage neutralize the gate-drain parasitic capacitance and for voltage gain improvement. Besides, auxiliary transistor is employed to improve the small-signal linearity, i.e., the input third-order intercept point (IIP3). Implemented in 40nm CMOS technology, the proposed LNA achieves an input-impedance matching (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) <-8.7dB and power gain of 7.7-to-10.7dB when covering 18.6-to-27.6GHz. The IIP3 is >-3.1dBm and the minimum NF is 4dB. The LNA consumes 16.3mW from 1.1V power supply and occupies 0.11mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> active area.

articleTitle: A Switched Capacitor Converter with Open Circuit Voltage MPPT Method for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 7-phase switched capacitor converter with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for piezoelectric energy harvester. The switched capacitor converter achieves the fractional open-circuit voltage MPPT method by reconstructing the capacitor array according to the appropriate voltage conversion ratio (VCR) to improve the mechanical energy harvesting efficiency in complex scenarios. The 7-phase switched capacitor converter designed in this paper can achieve voltage conversion ratios of 1/5, 1/3, 2/5, 1/2, 3/5, 2/3, and 4/5. Designed the switched capacitor converter in a 180 nm CMOS process. The simulation result shows when the vibration frequency changes, the overall efficiency of the proposed circuit can reach 80.66%.

articleTitle: Acceleration of ResNet18 Based on Run-time Inference Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: ResNet18 is a deep convolutional neural network that belongs to the ResNet (Residual Network) family. Due to its excellent performance and relatively shallow network depth, it has a wide and flexible range of applications, particularly excelling in scenarios where computational resources are limited but high precision is required. It is widely used in image classification, object detection, and real-time applications in computer vision. This paper implements the acceleration of the ResNet18 network using an inference engine and compares the results. Experimental result shows that when using the inference engine for acceleration, inference speed is significantly improved in all precision levels, with particularly notable improvements in INT8 precision.

articleTitle: Hardware Design and Security Analysis for SHA-256 in PQC Sphincs+
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The development of quantum computers poses significant threats and challenges to modern cryptography, leading to the emergence of post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. Currently, the post-quantum SPHINCS+ algorithm has been listed by NIST as one of the four standardized algorithms. This paper focuses on the hardware implementation of one of the underlying algorithms for the SPHINCS+ algorithm, specifically the SHA-256 algorithm. Since all components used in the signature process are computed using the SHA-256 algorithm, there is an urgent need to design a high-throughput SHA-256 algorithm dedicated to the SPHINCS+ algorithm. This paper presents a SHA-256 algorithm design with a throughput of up to 2844-Mbps at a clock frequency of 100-MHz, utilizing the SAKURA-G FPGA as the implementation and verification platform. This paper also extracted and analyzed the power consumption of the hardware code, proposing the addition of data masking operations to make it difficult to extract critical data from power consumption curves. Through verification, the SHA-256 design presented in this paper is suitable for the postquantum SPHINCS+ algorithm.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity, Conflict-Free Memory Access Scheme for Flexible NTT /INTT Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) and inverse NTT (INTT) are widely used to accelerate polynomial multi-plications in lattice-based cryptosystems. This paper proposes a low-complexity coefficient memory access pattern for an in-place NTT/INTT design. It simplifies the data path between the processing elements (PEs) and the memory banks. Moreover, to avoid read-after-write conflicts and achieve minimal (I)NTT computing cycles, we present a strategy that dynamically calculates and inserts necessary idle cycles during (I)NTT processing. Based on the proposed low-complexity and conflict-free memory access scheme, we develop a flexible NTT/INTT unified architecture. Our design allows the configuration of various parameter sets and parallelism setups at compile-time, while supporting polynomials of multiple degrees and moduli of different sizes at run-time. Experimental results on FPGA show that our design achieves better area efficiency and flexibility compared with previous works.

articleTitle: A Novel Current-Mode COT-Controlled Buck Converter for Phase-Interleaved Parallel Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a parallel current-mode COT-mode BUCK converter circuit is proposed for the problems of uneven load current distribution and large output ripple that may occur in the parallel connection of buck DC-DCs. The converter employs a programmable phase-shifting circuit based on the COT mode, which allows multiple phase differences to be set for the switching cycles of each parallel branch, enabling the inductor current currents of each parallel converter to achieve a balanced interleaving capability from 2-phase to 12-phase, which minimizes the output voltage ripple and improves the load response speed. The designed converter has been circuit and layout designed based on the Hitek <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18\mu \mathrm{m}30\mathrm{V}$</tex> BCD process. Simulation results show that the input voltage is 4V to 20V, the single-phase output current is 5A, the dual-phase parallel output current is 10A, the operating frequency range is 800kHz to 2MHz, and the dual-phase parallel connection can reduce the output voltage ripple from 5.016 m V to 1. 737m V compared with single-phase. The converter has a high conversion efficiency under light load conditions and up to 91<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>under heavy load conditions (VouT=3.3V, ILoAD=5A). The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed phase shift circuit.

articleTitle: RTplace: A Reinforcement Learning-based Macro Placement Method with ResNet and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As the scale and complexity of integrated circuit design continue to expand, automated chip placement technology has become crucial for enhancing design efficiency, reducing costs, and optimizing chip performance. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning-based macro placement method, which combines ResNet with Transformer, which autonomously generates high-quality chip placements through a global and local feature fusion approach(RTplace). RTplace embeds Transformer into ResNet structure to obtain different types of features. Additionally, a multi-level feature fusion module is introduced to achieve the fusion of global and local features. The pro-posed method captures information that might be lost during feature propagation and enhances the quality of placement. The experimental results indicate that RTplace has better placement performance compared to other existing methods.

articleTitle: Surface Plasmon-Enhanced $\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$-Based MISIM Solar-Blind Photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> is one of the best materials for solar-blind ultraviolet photodetectors because of its suitable band gap (~4.9 eV) and high breakdown field strength (8 MV/cm). However, photodetectors based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> still suffer from the problem of relatively low light absorption efficiency. In order to improve the absorption efficiency, a new metal-insulator-semiconductor-insulator-metal (MISIM) type photodetector is proposed here, which is composed of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> film, a passivation layer of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex>, and an outer metal layer of metal nanoparticles (NPs). The metal which shows strong surface plasmon resonance (SPR) coupling effect with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> films is chosen according to the dispersion relations. Calculation results show that Al NPs is the best choice. Furthermore, the impact of various sizes of Al NPs on the performance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> based photodetectors is systematically studied using the finite difference time domain (FDTD). Simulation results show that Al NPs with a radius of 50 nm can significantly enhance the absorption efficiency of the MISIM-type photodetector within the wavelength range of 200 nm to 300 nm, with the absorption efficiency increasing from 0.1 to 0.3. Notably, the absorption efficiency increased even by 85% at the wavelength of 254 nm. These findings pave the way of fabricating high performance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> photodetectors by decorating metal nanostructures based on localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effects.

articleTitle: A Low Power Frequency Synthesizer with Dual-Path Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, we present a frequency synthesizer for low-voltage applications, utilizing a dual-path charge-pump phase-locked loop (PLL) architecture. The proportional path charge pump is designed with a IUP charge-only structure, which alleviates the need for stringent current matching in the charge pump (CP). As a result, there is no need for current mismatch suppression techniques, leading to lower power consumption and simplifying the circuit design of the CP. The VCO features a ring oscillator that is both compact and energy-efficient, leveraging its self-generated multi-phase outputs to achieve frequency tripling, which further reduces power consumption.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Low-Noise Low-Offset Comparators for High-Performance ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The need for low-power high-resolution analog-to-digital converter (ADC) used in dynamic sensors is pushing towards the use of low-noise and low-offset dynamic comparators to improve power efficiency and speed. In this paper, we have compared state-of-the-art dynamic comparators which focus on low-noise and low-offset. They are designed in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS technology. StrongARM (SA) latch with embedded preamplifier achieves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$120-\mu \mathrm{V}$</tex> input-referred noise while consuming only 1 pJ per comparison under 1.85-V supply. SA with Floating Inverter Amplifier (FIA) has lowest figure of merit (FOM) which represents the power efficiency of a comparator. Based on the simulation & analysis results, we demonstrate SA latch with embedded preamplifier and SA latch with FIA are good candidates for low-power high-resolution analog-to-digital converter (ADC).

articleTitle: A Power Balanced Against Side Channel Attack SM4 Algorithm Based on RRAM/CMOS Hybrid Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The SM4 algorithm is now widely used to ensure the security of data transmission, but its physical implementation is still vulnerable to side channel attack. By studying the structure of SM4 algorithm, this paper proposes a scheme of SM4 algorithm against side-channel attack based on RRAM/CMOS hybrid power balancing. The scheme first studies the dynamic power balancing mechanism under the cooperative operation mode of RRAM cell and CMOS, and designs the complementary output RRAM/CMOS hybrid power balancing cell circuit by utilizing the RRAM programmable resistor states and the efficient control of CMOS logic gates; then, the leakage analysis reveals that there is a vulnerability of SM4 algorithm hardware implementation in the wheel output. To address this issue, the power balancing cell circuit is applied to the wheel output position of SM4 algorithm to decouple the correlation between power consumption and data in the output stage; finally, the power consumption curve is extracted by Spectre simulation under TSMC 65nm process and verified against correlation power analysis (CPA) attack. The experimental results demonstrate that, compared with the traditional implementation, the circuit proposed in this paper can still defend against CPA attack with 1200 power consumption curves, with more than two times higher hardware security than the traditional SM4 implementation.

articleTitle: The Investigation of AlGaN Grown by MBE by PL and Time-resolved PL
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The influence of growth temperature on the crystalline quality and optical properties of AlGaN grown using plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), was investigated. The growth temperature exhibited a significant impact on the growth mode and surface morphology. Specifically, at a growth temperature of 750 degrees Celsius, when appropriate Al and Ga flow rates were employed, the AlGaN layer exhibited exceptional surface morphology and favorable optical properties. The optical properties of the AlGaN material were explored, revealing the presence of two distinct non-radiative recombination centers characterized by different activation energies. The minority carrier lifetimes were measured as 560 ps at 10 K and 64 ps at room temperature. The underlying mechanism was analyzed from the perspective of carrier dynamics, shedding light on the observed phenomena.

articleTitle: A Low-Power 50 Gb/s PAM4 High-Speed SerDes Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: For high-speed serial interface transmitter applications, this paper presents the design of a 50 Gb/s low-power 3-tap/4-tap configurable forward feedback equalization (FFE) four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) high-speed serial interface (SerDes) transmitter based on UMC 28 nm CMOS technology. The design adopts a half-rate PAM4 transmitter architecture. The design ingeniously replaces the traditional power-hungry current-mode logic (CML) structure with C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>MOS latches and selectors, facilitating data delay and rate synthesis before the data reaches the combined driver. This approach significantly reduces the transmitter's power consumption. The configurable 3-tap/4-tap FFE fine-tunes the equalization coefficients using a digital-to-analog converter (DAC), ensuring optimal signal integrity. Moreover, the output driver utilizes inductive peaking technology to extend the bandwidth, crucial for maintaining high-speed data transmission. Simulation results show that at 1.05 V supply voltage, the differential output eye height for 50 Gb/s PAM4 output is 86 mV with an eye width of 20.8 ps (0.52 UI) and the power consumption of 71.58 mW (energy efficiency is 1.4316 pJ/bit) when the 3-tap FFE is in use. The differential output eye height is 90 mV with an eye width of 20.8 ps (0.52 UI) and the power consumption of 72.99 mW (energy efficiency is 1.4598 pJ/bit) when the 4-tap FFE is in use. The overall layout area of the transmitter is 0.036 mm”.

articleTitle: Antenna Far-field Test System and Signal Processing Based on UAV Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In antenna performance testing, near-field testing is less reliable than far-field testing due to various factors. This system uses the UAV to carry an omnidirectional antenna that matches the antenna to be tested. When drone moves in a circle around the antenna, the antenna under test receives the signal from the transmitting antenna and transmits the signal to the data acquisition board. The data acquisition board transmits the data to the PC in real time through the gigabit network port, and processes the received data on the PC and draws the signal time domain diagram and frequency domain diagram. The directional diagram also requires the GPS coordinates of the drone's flight. This system provides great convenience for the tester.

articleTitle: An AGC-PI Based Readout Circuit for Resonant Pressure Microsensor
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a readout circuit based on AGC-PI structure for resonant pressure microsensors. A Gm-C based PI controller, which consists of an operational trans-conductance amplifier and a resistor-capacitor network, realizes the proportional-integral control and error amplification. An MOS resistor divider is used as VGA for its simple structure and low flicker noise. The readout circuit is fabricated in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> BCD process. Experiments show that the system can operate at temperatures from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-55\sim 85^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and supply voltages from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\sim 5.5\mathrm{V}$</tex> with a bias instability of 0. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$024\text{Hz}$</tex> and a phase noise of -100dBc/Hz. The current consumption is 2. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7\text{mA}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\mathrm{V}$</tex> supply voltage.

articleTitle: Package Design and Reliability Verification of Spaceborne SiP
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: System-in-Package (SiP) refers to the integration of multiple functional chips onto the same substrate through micro-assembly to achieve systematic functionality. It boasts advantages such as small physical dimensions, high packaging efficiency, good compatibility, and low power consumption. As a core control component crucial to the normal operation of satellites in orbit, on-board processors require not only high performance but also high integration and small size. The application of SiP in on-board processors to form a microsystem can better meet their high-performance demands for miniaturization and functional integration. However, with the increase in integration and signal frequency, the operating voltage of chips has decreased, necessitating the consideration of signal integrity and power stability issues in SiP to ensure its reliability. Additionally, due to the need for long-term reliability of aerospace SiP in specific environments, it is necessary to optimize packaging processes, improve SiP heat dissipation, and enhance mechanical stability. In this paper, we designed a microsystem SiP for on-board processors and conducted simulation analysis on its signal integrity, power integrity, heat dissipation, and stress, verifying that the reliability of the SiP meets the reference standards.

articleTitle: A Flexible Routing Strategy Based on Region Manager in Network-on-Chip for Neural Network Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In contemporary neuromorphic acceleration systems, the diversity of neural network models and their corre-sponding network mappings engenders a variety of data flow patterns and transaction sizes. The heterogeneity of these models necessitates tailored routing methodologies. In this paper, we commence with an examination of prevalent traffic patterns in-herent in cutting-edge neuromorphic accelerators. Subsequently, we introduce a routing strategy predicated on configurable region managers. These managers not only ensure deadlock-free routing paths by monitoring network conditions but are also capable of adapting to disparate traffic patterns through the deployment of versatile routing configurations. Through simulations, we have ascertained that our proposed architecture can markedly diminish data latency by 4% to 39% and improve throughput up to 44%, representing a significant enhancement over the conventional mesh network-on-chip (NoC) designs that are currently in widespread use.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on the SRAMs Based on III-V Homojunction and Heterojunction TFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Although Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors (TFETs) are acknowledged for energy-efficient devices, their low on-state current significantly constrains their development. In contrast to conventional TFETs, III-V heterojunction TFETs demonstrate steeper switching characteristics and higher on-state currents. This paper employs a semi-empirical Verilog-A compact model to conduct a comparative analysis of the performance of 8T SRAM cells utilizing GaAsSb/InGaAs heterojunction and InGaAs homojunction TFETs through Spectre simulation. The results reveal that, compared to the homojunction configuration, SRAM cells based on heterojunction TFETs exhibit a marked decrease in read/write delay but an increase in read/write power consumption, with no significant change in noise margin. This suggests a trade-off between speed and power performance metrics in the design of SRAM cells utilizing heterojunction TFETs. Furthermore, the variability of SRAM based on these two types of TFETs is analyzed, indicating that SRAM utilizing the heterojunction structure is more susceptible to process variations.

articleTitle: 32Gb/s Low-Power NRZ Signal Serdes Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a SerDes receiver for receiving 32Gb/s non-return-to-zero (NRZ) signals is designed with a half-rate structure to reduce the power consumption of the circuit, and the equalisation scheme is a continuous-time linear equaliser (CTLE) and a 2-tap decision feedback equaliser (DFE) equalisation. In order to extend the high-frequency bandwidth and increase the high-frequency gain, a CTLE with Gm-TIA structure is designed; in order to reduce the power consumption, an improved StrongARM comparator and a TSPC-type D flip-flop (DFF) are designed. Using 28nm CMOS process, under 1.05/1.2V supply voltage, the post-simulation results show that: at Nyquist 16GHz frequency, the CTLE can compensate 17.42dB channel attenuation; the variable gain amplifier (VGA) can improve 12.82dB low-frequency gain, and the eye-width after DFE equalisation is O.77UI, and the eye-height is 385mV; the overall power consumption at the receiver side is 20.25mW, energy efficiency is 0.63pJ/bit, and the area of the layout core is 0.096mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed circuit is suitable for use in high speed serial interface and communication applications.

articleTitle: Single-event Effect Simulation Platform for Space Processors
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the space environment, space processors are highly susceptible to single-event effects that can flip or latch the contents of logic units in the processor, leading to processor failure. Before carrying out processor fault-tolerant design, an in-depth single-event sensitivity analysis is required, especially to simulate the behavioral characteristics of the processor in the presence of single-event effects. To address this need, this paper presents a single-event effect simulation platform for SPARC architecture processor models. The platform adopts the Unified Command-line Interface to simulate the single event effect in the operation of the space processor, and makes use of Makefile and Python to realize the automatic injection of faults caused by the single event effect; by loading the test cases simulating the single event effect, it simulates the single event effect during the operation of the space processor, and optimizes the simulation flow so as to reduce the simulation time.

articleTitle: A Computing-in-Memory Architecture with High Precision and High Linear MAC Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a computing-in-memory (CIM) architecture with high precision and high linearity multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations for deep neural networks (DNNs). The CIM array is composed of 12T SRAM cells, and the 8-bit input is divided into high 4-bit and low 4-bit, which are respectively fed into the cells of two adjacent columns. The multiplication results of the cells are accumulated on the compute bit lines (CBLs) and quantized by 4-bit Single-Slope analog-to-digital converters (SS ADCs). In the UMC 110nm process with a power supply of 1.2V, the circuit implements convolution operations with 8-bit input and 8-bit weight for a 3×3 convolution kernel, resulting in a 20-bit full precision output. The simulation results indicate that the proposed CIM architecture achieves a maximum nonlinearity error of only 0.83% for MAC operations, demonstrating high linearity. Moreover, it ensures excellent linearity and accuracy of output results in the presence of process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations.

articleTitle: A Low Power BLE-Compatible Wake-Up Receiver Achieving -85-dBm Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article presents a wake-up receiver (WuRX) compatible with Bluetooth-Low-Energy(BLE). The wake-up receiver (WuRX) fabricated in a 55-nm CMOS process and operates from a 0.7-V supply. A WuRX with a gain-programmable amplifier (PGA) provides a gain range of 21dB. It achieves a sensitivity of -85dBm, while consuming 167uW via using passive circuits and poly phase filter (PPF).

articleTitle: Variable Gain Phase Shifter Design for Millimeter Wave Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The front end of the transceiver of the traditional RF phase-shifting architecture contains independent phase shifters and attenuators, so the transceiver channel of the RF phase-shifting architecture phased array system has the disadvantages of large area and high loss. In this paper, with the goal of solving the problem of large transceiver channel area and high power consumption of the traditional RF phase-shifting phased array system, the research contents of passive device modeling technology, orthogonal amplitude phase control technology and linear phase control technology are completed through the joint design of the phase shifter and the variable gain amplifier, and the variable gain phase shifter with orthogonal amplitude phase control capability is realized, and the linear phase control is realized based on the symmetry of gain and phase in the vector sum phase shifter, which greatly improves the accuracy of phase control.

articleTitle: A Defense Against Rowhammer Attacks Based on Dual-Layer RRAM Counting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The security issues in high-density memory have attracted increasing attention, and how to defend Row Hammer (RH) has become a research hotspot. To address the issue of significant storage overhead in defending RH attacks, this paper proposes a defense method based on dual-layer counting with Resistive Random Access Memory (RRAM). Initially, this method investigates the transition from low-resistance state to high-resistance state in RRAM, and utilizes the resistance variation process of RRAM to represent the number of row activations, achieving the functionality of counting row activations using a single RRAM; Secondly, a group counter is formed by an RRAM that one end connected to multiple memory rows and a sensitive amplifier that monitors the resistance variation of the RRAM. This group counter completes the aggregated counting of the row groups formed by multiple memory rows, completing the aggregation counting of the row groups composed of multiple memory rows; Finally, a row counter is constructed using RRAM and a sensitive amplifier placed at the end of a single memory row to accurately count the memory rows that exceed the counting range of the previous stage, achieving protection against RH. The dual-layer counter composed of row counter and group counter is connected to DRAM and tested under TSMC28nm technology. The experimental results demonstrate that the two counters can work together to protect against RH attacks without affecting the original Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) timing logic.

articleTitle: Design of A Programmable Digital Controller System on Chip for Switching Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A programmable digital controller for DC-DC switching converters has the advantages of strong versatility and high stability. In this paper, a programmable System on Chip (SoC) of digital controller is designed for applying to more switching converters topologies. Based on ARM Cortex-M0 processor, this digital controller SoC includes three error amplifying analog-to-digital converters (EADC) with 6 bits, four DPWMs with 250ps resolution, three PID control loops, and some digital peripherals that can achieve real-time monitoring, peripheral configuration, and management communication functions. Fabricated in a 110nm CMOS process. The experimental results show that by reasonably configuring the parameters of the registers, this chip can control a full bridge converter to achieve the design requirements, which proved strong versatility of this chip.

Author Keywords: Hard Switched Full Bridge Switching Converters

articleTitle: Pattern Recognization of Instruction-Level Power Noise with Sythesized Sensor Inside FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In a multitenant FPGA, the power noise induced by a victim circuit form a side channel for an attacker on the same FPGA chip to steal the information of the victim.
