Previous researches are performed on program-level to show how the algorithm type or the key data of a victim can be identified through a synthesized on-chip noise sensor. This paper is focused on the fine-grained waveform of the power noise that correspond to single instructions of the microprocessor. The purpose is to see whether the instruction type can be identified through the synthesized sensor. A MIPS center processor unit (CPU) is designed as the victim. A ring oscillator (RO) based sensor called Flexible-RO is designed as the attacker. Both of them are implemented in a Xilinx Artix-7 xc7a200tfbg676 FPGA. The waveforms of the supply voltage of 37 different instructions are collected. Correlation analysis shows that many instructions have power pattern that are distinguishable from those of other instructions. Power patterns of memory-type instructions are different from the arithmetic and logic instructions. The observation made in this paper indicates that, from the privacy point of view, a remote attacker can easily determine the instruction level details of operation of the victim circuit. The conclusion of the paper helps understanding the bottom mechanism of security issues of the multitenant FPGA.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a New Type of Electrothermal Micro-flat Lens Unit Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on the principle of electrothermal actuator, this paper designs a new type of electrothermal micro-flat lens unit structure to micro-adjust the phase of the transmitted beam. This structure mainly consists of a micro-flat lens and four symmetrical S-shaped actuators. The lens can realize two motion states, vertical displacement and tilting, by applying voltages to different actuators. Symmetry of actuators avoids the influence of ambient temperature on the tilt of the lens. A positive hexagonal shape of lens provides a foundation for relevant dense array structure with a high filling factor. The natural frequency, displacement and tilting of the structure are simulated by COMSOL. Results show that the electrothermal micro-flat lens unit structure can work normally lower than 5806.8 HZ, and get a large vertical displacement of 166 µm and a tilt of 12° at a low driving voltage of 1.8 V.

articleTitle: A Sinusoial Signal Generation IC for Bioimpedance Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a sinusoidal voltage and current generation integrated circuit suitable for bioimpedance measurement. The circuit mainly consists of a voltage-controlled oscillator, a waveform conversion module, and a current driver. This circuit is designed to generate a sinusoidal current signal with three adjustable frequencies, 300 Hz, 1 KHz, and 3 KHz, suitable for bioimpedance measurement. The sinusoidal current generation chip is implemented in SMIC 0.18-µm CMOS process, with a core area of 0.062mm2. Measurement results validate the function of the chip. The output voltage and current amplitude are 140 mV and 50 nA, respectively. The circuit's power consumption is 281 µW, under the power supply voltage of 1.8V. The output frequency error is within 3.3%.

articleTitle: A 56-Gbaud PAM4 Analog Adaptive Equalizer in 90-nm BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 56-Gbaud PAM4 analog adaptive equalizer is designed in 90-nm BiCMOS technology. The designed analog adaptive equalizer consists of an equalizer, a power detector, an error amplifier, and a charge pump. The equalizer is composed of a continuous-time linear equalizer and a low-frequency equalizer, and it is capable of simultaneously compensating for the losses of the signal at low, medium and high frequencies. The spectrum balancing scheme based on power detection is adopted to achieve adaptation. It can adaptively compensate for different attenuation channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the adaptive equalizer effectively compensates for channel losses ranging from 4.5dB to 8.5dB at 28GHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Bitline Repeater For High Reliable Nonvolatile RRAM-based FPGA Configuration Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Nonvolatile SRAM (NVSRAM) has garnered significant attention over the past few years for its integration of high-speed write/read capabilities of SRAM and the nonvolatile cells. However, research on integrating NVSRAM into radiation-hardened systems, which demand high reliability, remains limited. FPGA is key components in space electronic systems, with their configuration memory playing a vital role in enabling programmable logic, and its ability to resist interference is crucial. While NVSRAM based on RRAM can significantly enhance the interference resistance, the write currents are considerably higher than SRAM, leading to a pronounced IR drop on the bitline, and it can easily cause write failures as parallelism increases. To address the issues, this study proposes a novel bitline repeater for RRAM-based FPGA configuration memory. By connecting in parallel on the bitline, the impact of IR drop can be significantly mitigated, leading to a potential multiplication in the number of configuration memory cells. The simulation results demonstrate that the repeater circuit can resist high-energy particles interference with the charge exceeding 100pC, which corresponds to a Linear Energy Transfer (LET) threshold exceeding 10000 MeV·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg.

articleTitle: The MBIST Implementation of SoC Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of memory on SoC (System on Chip) chips, Memory Built-in Self Test (MBIST) has become a crucial component of Design for Testability (DFT) in SoC chip design. In this paper, MBIST design is based on a SoC chip in SMIC40nm process, which reuses the JTAG(Joint Test Action Group) interface and PLL(Phase-Locked Loop) on the SoC chip. The MBIST design can complete the at-speed test of all the SRAMs in the SoC chip design, which is implemented following the flow of Tessent Shell MemoryBIST. Through MBIST simulation verification and wafer test after chip fabrication, the effectiveness of MBIST circuit in screening the SoC chip's memory is demonstrated, leading to improved efficiency in chip application test.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Low-Power Differential Ring Voltage Controlled Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work presents a low-power, low noise, and high output swing four stage ring oscillator (VCO). By reducing the total thermal noise current injected into the output node of the VCO during the transition period of output voltage swing, and improving the performance of phase noise by using a feedforward path and a new auxiliary input to increase the output voltage swing of the oscillator, the corresponding power consumption is reduced. The TSMC 180nm 1P6M process was used for simulation, and the phase noise of the ring oscillator was -93dBc/Hz at a center frequency of 2GHz and an offset carrier frequency of 1MHz. And it only consumes 1.1 mA current, with an oscillator's FoM of 156.7dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: Research on Successive Approximation Analog-to-Digital Converter Circuit for Readout Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The imaging quality in an array detector is directly impacted by the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) unit: as detection arrays progress towards higher density, precision, and longer distances, the demands for ADC circuit accuracy and footprint become increasingly stringent. This study is centered on investigating and developing an Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) circuit tailored for the quantization of analog signals. Specific research areas include: (1) The development of a 12-bit Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC. This circuit employs bootstrap sampling switches, a timing sequence based on VCM-split capacitor array top-plate sampling, and utilizes multi-stage bridged capacitor arrays to significantly reduce capacitor footprint. (2) Incorporating bandgap and Low Dropout Regulator (LDO) circuits, the design of bias circuits for the system involves the utilization of a comparator reset clock to effectively govern the initiation of the bias circuit., thereby reducing circuit power consumption during comparator reset periods.

articleTitle: A Compact Elliptic Curve Cryptography Accelerator Over Prime Field for System-on-Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) is widely adopted for secure communications due to its efficiency and ro-bust security features. Despite its benefits, ECC's computational intensity, especially over prime fields, poses integration challenges for cost-sensitive System-on-Chips (SoC). This paper proposes a compact accelerator tailored for elliptic curve arithmetic oper-ations over prime fields. Verified on the Xilinx Virtex-7 FPGA platform, this ECC accelerator achieves point multiplication on the NIST curve P-256 in 18.0 ms, operating at 156.9 MHz and utilizing only 589 slices. An ASIC implementation of the 384-bit version accelerator has been integrated into a metering SoC on a 22-nm CMOS process. Operating at 400 MHz, it can achieve point multiplication on the NIST curve P-256 in 7.1 ms and on the NIST curve P-384 in 10.7 ms, utilizing 31K gate equivalents. Its low gate count combined with high performance makes it a good solution for enhancing the security capabilities of cost-sensitive SoCs.

articleTitle: A 12bit/100kHz Two-Step Single-Slope ADC for SWIR Image Sensor Based on CMOS 180nm Process
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 12bit/100kHz column-level two-step single-slope ADC (TS-SS ADC) designed for SWIR image sensor to achieve the area efficiency, high sensitivity and rapid response speed. The proposed ADC employs a dynamic adjustable reference voltage compensation and a four-terminal input comparator to enhance resolution and reduce charge leakage. The two-step architecture divides the quantization process into coarse and fine stages, significantly improving speed and precision. A prototype ADC was implemented in a 180nm CMOS technology, which achieves an SNDR of 72.7 dB and an SFDR of 80.7 dB under a 3.3V supply at a sampling frequency of 100 kS/s. The input voltage range is 1.7 V, with an ENOB of 11.78 bits. The ADC core occupies an active area of 0. 7226mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed ADC demonstrates superior performance for advanced SWIR imaging applications.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Dynamic Comparator Through Body-biasing and Clock Boosting
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A high speed dynamic comparator is proposed in this paper. The comparator features body biasing of the differential input transistors and clock boosting charge pump to enhance the transconductances adaptively, thereby accelerating comparison speed. The comparator exhibits low offset and is suitable for high-speed 8-bit SAR-ADC applications. Compared to the conventional double-tail comparator, the proposed design achieves a nearly 50% increase in speed and a 2x reduction in power consumption. Furthermore, compared with the conventional strong-arm latch based comparator, the proposed comparator achieves a 30% increase in speed at 40 nm SMIC process.

articleTitle: A Lightweight, Real-Time Die-to-Die Interface Protocol and Associated Adapter
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the reusable chiplet-based SoC design, efficient cross-die data transfer with standard die-to-die (D2D) interfaces requires the utilization of D2D adapters for conversion between on-chip bus and D2D physical interface as well as corresponding protocols. However, few designs satisfy the demands for low-cost, low-power, and high real-time. This paper introduces a lightweight, real-time chiplet interface protocol and its D2D adapter circuits for edge sensing applications. The D2D adapter supports multiplexing of AHB, APB and custom message on-chip protocols and differentiated treatment of them. To meet high real-time requirement, the design assigns fixed priorities and transaction types to different on-chip buses, while using Data Bus Inversion for low-power encoding. This design has been verified to achieve a latency of 7.48 ns and a power consumption of 3.096 mW, outperforming similar designs previously proposed.

articleTitle: Design of a 56-GBaud Low Noise PAM-4 Optical Receiver in 90-nm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 56 GBaud low noise PAM-4 transimpedance amplifier(TIA) is proposed in this paper. An shunt-feedback topology transimpedance amplifier(SF-TIA) integrated with a front-end auto gain control circuit(AGC1) can tolerant up to 1.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mA_{pp}$</tex> input current without distortion. A variable gain amplifier(VGA) with post AGC loop can maintain the amplitude of output swing at approximately 500 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mV_{pp}$</tex>. An output buffer designed with T-coil can provide good output matching performance. Designed in 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology, the low noise PAM-4 optical receiver has a maximum transimpedance gain of 79 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dB}\Omega$</tex> while -3 dB bandwidth is 36 GHz and input referred noise current is 2.33 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu A_{rms}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Polymer-Based Power OFETs with Floating Field Plate Structure Using Metal Mask Fabrication Process
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The polymer semiconductor diketopyrrolopyrrole thieno[3,2-b] thiophene (DPPT-TT) has been used to prepare organic power devices due to its excellent off-state breakdown performance. However, thinner organic semiconductor (OSC) layers can lead to premature breakdown due to the two-dimensional electric field crowding effect, causing electric field accumulation at the OSC and dielectric layer interface. To obtain a higher breakdown voltage (BV) by improving the electric field distribution, we designed a floating field plate lateral drift region organic field effect transistor (FFP-LDR-OFET). In this study, we fabricated and compared two types of devices with and without the floating field plate using the same process. The results show that the addition of the floating field plate increased the device's on-state saturation current from -0.7µA to-1. IµA, a 57.1% improvement, and the off-state breakdown voltage from 619V to 1880V, a 200% enhancement.

articleTitle: Dynamic Memristor-Based Reservoir Computing for Gesture Recognition Application
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In recent years, brain-inspired computing has garnered widespread research interest. Compared to traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs), reservoir computing (RC) is a low training cost network that efficiently processes temporal signals. A key challenge in hardware implementation is generating a rich reservoir state. In this work, we report a dynamic memristor-based reservoir computing system that achieves diverse reservoir states through a time division multiplexing masking process. By using an AgInSbTe (AIST) layer in electrochemical metallization (ECM) memory, we demonstrate substantial potential for stable RC. This AIST-based RC systems exhibits nonlinearity, cycling stability, and relatively low average power consumption, meeting the requirements of RC systems. The system achieves a gesture recognition accuracy of up to 96%. Our work could pave the way for future efficient memristor-based RC systems capable of handling more complex temporal tasks.

articleTitle: A Low Power Low Noise High Speed Comparator for Asynchronous SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a high speed, low power and low noise comparator for asynchronous SAR ADC use. In the proposed comparator, several techniques are used to improve the performance. The input pair of preamplifier are directly connected to the latch to improve the speed, and the stacked clocked tail technique is proposed to cut off the leakage path to save power, simultaneously enhancing the input transistors' gm/Id, thereby reducing the input referred noise. To alleviate the load of output nodes and enhance speed, an additional latch is added to isolate the large parasitic capacitance of the input transistors from comparator output. The post layout simulation result shows that in 28nm CMOS technology, with supply of 1V, the proposed comparator consumes only 45.73fJ energy per comparison with 10G clock. The input referred noise of comparator is 0.75mVrms and CLK-Q delay is 29.79ps. The FOM value is very competitive compared to the comparators presented latest.

articleTitle: A 0.4 to 10.8GHz, +20dBm OIP3 Broadband Switchable Differential to Single-Ended Active Balun in 130-nm BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 0.4-10.8 GHz active balun in 130nm SiGe BiCMOS technology is presented. The balun realizes differential to single-ended (D2S) conversion using two paths, one with common collector (CC) structure and the other with common emitter (CE) structure. The CE path, together with the bias circuit, constructs a proportional current mirror that makes the balun switchable. In order to make the two input impedances as equal as possible, the emitter follower (EF) structure is adopted as the buffer. The bond wire inductance and package parasitic parameters are considered to be a part of the output matching network (OMN) to enhance the bandwidth (BW). Designed in 130-nm BiCMOS process, this work achieves 3-dB BW of 0.4-10.8 GHz, an output compression point (OP1dB) of 8.9dBm, third-order intercept point (OIP3) of 20.7dBm at 1GHz, respectively. The maximum phase error of the active balun is 4 degrees and the maximum amplitude error is 1.7 dB over 0.4-10.8 GHz frequency range. The chip area is 0.105 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a static power consumption of 66mW.

articleTitle: A Digital Power Amplifier Based on Voltage-Control Linearization Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 10 GHz digital power amplifier (DPA) based on voltage-control linearization (VCL) technique in 65 nm bulk CMOS. The nonlinearity mechanisms are analyzed, and the VCL technique is adopted to push the transistors of on-state DPA cell into saturated region to suppress the nonlinearity. Besides, the transformer-based output matching network is utilized for high efficiency. The proposed DPA achieves maximum AM-AM distortion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.75\mathbf{dB}$</tex> and maximum AM-PM distortion of 7.5°, and delivers a saturated power of 24.0 dBm with drain efficiency of 41.8% at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: A 24-30 GHz Image-Rejection Filtering LNA with > 35-dBc Image-Rejection Ratio at < 22 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper introduces a 24–30 GHz Image-rejection filtering Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) for millimeter-wave super-heterodyne receivers, employing 0.15µm GaAs pHEMT technology and targeting n257 and n258 bands. We propose an innovative design approach to integrate multiple Elliptic High-pass Filters directly into the LNA's matching network. This is achieved through the integration of three additional capacitors into the LNA's original matching network, which effectively generate three transmission zeros in the lower frequency, resulting in a pronounced Elliptic High-pass Filter response. This novel circuit topology significantly improves the attenuation rate of the LNA's gain outside its operational frequency band, achieving more than 35 dBc of rejection at the image frequency below 22 GHz. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed LNA achieves a Noise Figure (NF) of less than 1.9 dB, a linear gain of 21.3±1.3 dB, input and output return losses of less than -12 dB, and an Output 1dB compression point (OP1dB) exceeding 10 dBm, making it suitable for millimeter-wave satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: A Low Power, Wide Band Robust Startup Class C DCO with High Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A robust starting complementary Class C DCO with low phase noise and low power consumption is designed by 40 nm process. The frequency modulation accuracy of the DCO is improved by using a mismatched capacitor pair structure on the inverted PMOS varactor. The tuning bank of this DCO consists of a 6-bit band-tuning capacitor array, a 4-bit coarse-tuning capacitor array, a 4-bit medium-tuning capacitor array, and a 4-bit fine-tuning capacitor array, which can obtain a frequency tuning range of 9.6 GHz to 10.5 GHz; and a two-bit PVT capacitor array is also used to cope with the variation of different process angles. The robust start-up circuit mainly consists of an amplitude detection circuit and a comparator to control the gate voltage of the cross-coupled NMOS transistor. Simulation results show that the DCO has a minimum tuning accuracy of 4.95 kHz, a phase noise of −114.114dBc/Hz@1MHz, and a power consumption of 10.02mW at a frequency of 9.6 GHz with a supply voltage of 1.8V. The FOM value is 183.75.

articleTitle: An Active Gate Driver with Controllable Gate Current for SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An active gate driver (AGD) with controllable gate current (CGC) for SiC MOSFETs is proposed to reduce voltage overshoots and current overshoots. In the CGC-AGD, the controllable current overshoot suppression circuit and voltage overshoot suppression circuit are designed to control the rate of changes in current (di/dt) and voltage (dv/dt) to effectively reduce overshoots. Meanwhile, the current conversion circuit and the push-pull amplifier circuit compensate for the current reduction resulting from the overshoot suppression. This paper simulated the current and voltage overshoot during the switching process based on a double pulse test set up with a 1200V SiC MOSFET by LTspice software. The simulation results show that the current overshoot was reduced by 60% and the voltage overshoot was reduced by 22% when compared to the conventional gate driver (CGD). While compared with the AGD circuit, the current overshoot of CGC-AGD is reduced by 26% and the voltage overshoot is reduced by 19%. These results demonstrate that the CGC-AGD has better suppress on current and voltage overshoot.

articleTitle: A High-reliability Au Stud Bump Bonding Strategy Based on Au Pads for Flip-chip Bonding Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Flip-chip bonding technology has been widely used in advanced packaging applications, where the Au stud bump bonding shows advantages in both the simple and flexible fabrication process and the good electrical performance. However, conventional Al pads suffer from long-term reliability risks due to the Au-Al inter metallic compounds (IMCs). In this paper, Au pads are fabricated on Al pads to provide an inherently stable Au-Au bonding interface for the Au stud bump bonding. The key parameters in the bonding process are investigated by the orthogonal experiments based on the bonding pressure, ultrasound power, and bonding time. According to the results of the shear force tests, the bonding time has the largest influence on the bonding strength, and the optimal process parameters are bonding pressure of 35 gf, ultrasonic power of 390 mW, and bonding time of 20 ms. Furthermore, reliability tests including the high-temperature storage tests (HTSTs) and the temperature cycling tests (TCTs) are carried out on the fabricated heterogeneous bonding structure, which demonstrates good reliability with average shear strengths of 42.65 gf and 43.30 gf after the HTSTs and the TCTs, respectively. This stable and reliable bonding strategy is beneficial to enhancing the reliability of the flip-chip bonding applications.

articleTitle: A Configurable Real-Time Self-Test and Repair Engine for Improving the Reliability and Functional Safety of RAM Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Hard and soft errors in embedded memories have become a serious reliability issue in IoT, industrial, automotive, and other devices with stringent requirements for operating environments and reliability. A configurable self-test and repair engine is proposed to detect and repair hard errors and correct soft errors in RAM arrays on-the-fly. This scheme effectively utilizes SRAM access intervals to achieve real-time self-test and repair with configurable self-test mode, address range, and repair depth. Estimated based on the existing failure model, this scheme significantly reduces the failure rate of RAM arrays with good practicability and small hardware overhead. Evaluated with TSMC's 40nm standard CMOS technology, the implementation with 8-address repair depth for (16384×39)-bit RAM array has a lightweight feature of 4640.261 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is only 1.68% of the RAM array area. In the case study on the FPGA platform with an embedded RISC- V core, the results show that the proposed engine causes a certain amount of increase in overhead, but almost no loss in system frequency and SRAM access efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Storage Network Architecture Simulator for Group Convolution Feature Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In group convolution, feature communication exhibits complex behaviors, leading to memory access becoming one of the factors limiting performance. For this issue, our team has proposed an on-chip storage network with adaptive bandwidth for centralized distributed storage. To verify the effectiveness of the storage network architecture and achieve rapid iteration towards the optimal architecture, this paper constructs behavioral models for group convolution computation units and storage networks based on SystemC and TLM, enabling rapid adjustment of the architecture and its models through parameters. Firstly, by analyzing the computational behavior of group convolution, we abstracted the basic behavioral model of the computation unit. Through this foundational model, complex computational behavior models for group convolution feature communication can be constructed. Secondly, we constructed models for the structures within the storage network, including routers, nodes, storage units, and bus bridges. Furthermore, an AXI interconnect model was built to facilitate data transfer between the memory access behavior model of group convolution and the storage network model. Through the storage network architecture simulator, read and write frequencies of network buses and nodes, as well as the storage utilization rates of each accessed network node, can be obtained to evaluate the performance of current architectural parameters and make appropriate adjustments to the architecture. The validity of the simulator in this paper was effectively verified through the simulation of 3×3 group convolution computation and a storage network architecture with four layers and five ports. The approach presented in this paper allows for rapid iteration of computational and storage architectures, as well as testing of iterative storage scheduling strategies, in problems characterized by complex memory access behaviors in group convolution feature communication.

articleTitle: A 10-bit 100MS/s SAR ADC with Optimized Power Efficiency in 28nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 10-bit 100 MS/s Successive Approximation Register Analog-to-Digital Converter (SAR ADC), fabricated in a 28nm CMOS process, that prioritizes low power consumption and high power efficiency. Employing techniques such as a double-bootstrapped switch, a dynamic comparator combined with a three-stage preamplifier structure, and a novel dynamic logic cell circuit. These known techniques are combined in a novel way to achieve specific performance goals such as low power consumption and optimized power efficiency. A superior balance between power consumption and performance has been found. At the same time, the challenges associated with small process sizes, such as increased leakage current and short-channel effects, are effectively improved in the 28nm CMOS process. Simulation results demonstrate that the designed SAR ADC meets design requirements with an Effective Number Of Bits (ENOB) of 8.35 bits, a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNDR) of 52.05 dB, and a Spurious-Free Dynamic Range (SFDR) of 69.48 dBc under a supply voltage of 0.9 V. It exhibits excellent performance and power efficiency, with an average power consumption of only 487 µW. This design achieves a balanced performance in signal acquisition and processing with moderate accuracy and speed, while emphasizing low power consumption, providing a solution that optimizes efficiency and performance for a broad range of technical applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Path-Sensitive Memory Dependence Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Memory dependence prediction is essential in superscalar out-of-order processors as it improves instruction-level parallelism efficiency by predicting dependencies between memory access instructions. However, existing state-of-the-art memory dependence predictors lack the ability to effectively utilize the dynamic execution information of conflicting instructions, leading to an excessive number of false positives and subsequently hindering overall performance. This work proposes Dynamic Path-Sensitive Memory Dependence Prediction (DPMDP), a novel dynamic path-sensitive memory dependence prediction method that dynamically selects the history length for each conflicting load instruction when multiple paths exist. Our key observation is that for load-store pairs with an initial occurrence of a violation if the conflicting store is waiting for an address translation that causes an execution delay, it does not create a dependency in the predictor initially and only creates it upon subsequent occurrences effectively. This observation is proven by running the SPEC CPU 2006 suite on the clock-accurate simulator GEM5. Through cycle-accurate simulation of the SPEC CPU 2006 suite, we show that DPMDP achieved an average performance improvement of 1.08% compared to Store Set and 13.06% compared to PHAST.

articleTitle: Critical Path Optimization for Logic Netlists
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: It is of great concern for high performance microprocessors to optimize logic delay and improve performance in the semi-custom design flow based on commercial standard cell library. To solve this issue, the paper proposes an automated method to optimize the delay of critical path in any block. Firstly, we construct the logic cone for critical paths based on the logic netlist obtained from semi-custom design flow. Secondly, the algorithm conducts large-scale graph partitioning on the logic cone with appropriate constraints. Thirdly, using two-level optimization, we perform logic restructuring on sub graphs resulting from partitioning to get a set of new logic cells. Finally, employing a match algorithm, we pick out high-reusable restructured logic cells for full-custom circuit implementation and replace corresponding circuit structures with them in the logic netlist. The proposed algorithm picks out 5 logic cells for restructuring. Experimental results demonstrate that the approach achieves a reduction in the logic levels and logic delay can be reduced by about 10% after replacing the corresponding structures in the logic netlist. The work effectively reduces critical path delay, which has the potential to enhance the performance of microprocessors.

articleTitle: Research Progress on the Readout Circuit of Superconducting Single-Photon Detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In recent years, superconducting single-photon detectors (SSPDs) have attracted extensive attention in the field of photoelectric detection due to their superior photoelectric properties. At present, the research on the optical properties of SSPDs is relatively mature, while the research on electrical properties still lacks a recognized theory. The readout circuit of SSPD is difficult to implement, and the design methods are incomplete. It is the prerequisite and essence for expanding the application scope of SSPD to understand in depth and develop the signal readout of SSPD. In this paper, we summarize the research progress of various readout circuits. Through the analysis and comparison of various readout schemes, the great development potential of low-temperature readout circuits for SSPDs was further prospected.

articleTitle: Improvement and Hardware Design of Image Denoising Algorithm Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Noise is always generated in the process of image generation and transmission, which hinders people from obtaining original image information, so image denoising has a wide range of applications. However, the image denoising algorithm based on deep learning has the disadvantages of large number of parameters and long inference time. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved lightweight neural network model in image denoising, compared with the DnCNN, saving up to 90.0% parameters in memory and increasing 21.4% inference speed. In addition, the cost and power consumption of commonly used neural network inference platforms (CPU, GPU) are relatively high, and it is difficult to deploy them in embedded devices. This paper completes the hardware implementation of the network structure through the Verilog hardware description language, and optimizes the resource occupation and circuit power consumption, and finally deploys the image denoising model on a FPGA. The experimental results show that the main frequency of the accelerator reaches 200 MHz, peak throughput is 200.207GOPS, and the energy consumption ratio is 17.183 GOPS/W, which is 1.9 times higher than the GPU and 26.2 times higher than the CPU.

articleTitle: HyperDMA: Enhancing High-Performance Computing and AI Workflows with Advanced Data Transfer Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the field of high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI), the performance and flexibility of direct memory access (DMA) controllers are crucial. This paper proposes a novel DMA architecture: HyperDMA, which achieves efficient data transfer and processing through a hierar-chical structure and a multi-core cooperative mechanism. Within HyperDMA, we design a data processing module that supports N -dimensional tensor transfer, gather transfer of non-contiguous source data, as well as broadcast and segmented transfer in a multi-core context. Finally, HyperDMA is integrated into the V-DSP computational core of the multi-core accelerator Fusion, and RTL simulation is performed using a simulation platform to evaluate its performance under different transfer modes and data granularities. The results show that HyperDMA significantly outperforms traditional DMA in data transfer efficiency and bandwidth utilization. Compared with not using HyperDMA, we achieve at least 39% performance improvement of GEMM algorithm. Compared with not using HyperDMA, we achieve at least 39% performance improvement of GEMM algorithm. This research provides an efficient and reliable solution for data transfer in HPC and AI applications.

articleTitle: A Configurable CORDIC and PSADIC Fusion Architecture for Nonlinear Edge-Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The computation of some crucial and nonlinear functions on the edge has to consider the area and latency. The traditional coordinate rotation digital computer (CORDIC) systems are widely used for these key functions, such as the sine, cosine, or the square root. For the co-calculations of the division and the square root, CORDIC requires more iteration cycles and resources, whereas the power series approximate digital computer (PSADIC) approach can half the iteration cycles. In this context, a configurable CORDIC and PSADIC fusion architecture is proposed here for edge-computing. It integrates five modes of CORDIC and PSADIC to calculate some crucial nonlinear functions. Each mode is simulated and verified on software and hardware, achieving the mean relative error distance (MRED) lower than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>. Under the TSMC 40nm process, the area of proposed architecture is increased by 18.3% compared to the PSADIC one, but the five modes, including all the calculations from CORDIC and PSADIC, are implemented.

articleTitle: DRV Prediction Using Quantum-Classical Hybrid Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In very large-scale integration (VLSI) design, accurately predicting design rule violation (DRV) before the routing stage has been a significant challenge. Traditional machine learning-based methods have shown promise but are often computationally intensive. This work first introduces the concept of incorporating quantum computing into DRV prediction through the development of a novel quantum-classical hybrid convolutional neural network, named QuDRV. The proposed model leverages the unique properties of quantum mechanics to perform convolution operations, which are particularly well-suited for handling the complex placement and routing correlations found in chip designs. Experimental results demonstrate that QuDRV achieves similar prediction accuracy while maintaining a simple network structure compared with classical counterparts. Although current quantum hardware limitations result in longer runtime, future advancements in quantum technology are expected to significantly improve both the accuracy and speed of QuDRV.

articleTitle: Exploration of Quantum Computing in Multi-Die FPGA Routing Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper delves into the innovative application of quantum computing to solve complex multi-die FPGA (FieldProgrammable Gate Array) routing challenges. Leveraging the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), we propose a novel approach that integrates classical routing techniques with quantum computing methodologies. This integration specifically utilizes QAOA to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the routing process. This hybrid approach partitions the routing task into intra-FPGA and inter-FPGA components, optimizing each segment through the appropriate computational techniques. Extensive experiments conducted on quantum computing simulators, alongside trials on actual quantum hardware, demonstrate the theoretical potential of quantum computing in enhancing the efficiency of multi-die FPGA routing solutions. Our findings suggest that despite the current limitations of quantum hardware, such as noise and error rates, quantum computing holds promise for advancing EDA methodologies. This paper contributes to the field by pioneering the integration of quantum algorithms with EDA techniques, offering a novel perspective on future applications of quantum computing in complex routing problems.

articleTitle: SER-NET: A Neuralize PCB Simulataneous Escape Routing Method Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Simultaneous escape routing is a challenging issue in PCB routing, as it involves the escape of pins within two integrated circuits (ICs) to boundaries under limited resources and net order constraints. With advancements in IC fabrication technologies, there has been an increase in the number of pins in ICs and a reduction in package size, further complicating the simultaneous escape problem in printed circuit boards (PCBs). Our approach addresses this problem by dividing it into two stages: escape endpoint assignment and end-to-end routing. We utilize graphical convolutional neural networks and attention-based networks to create policy and value models for specifying escape endpoints. These models learn PCB layouts and nets representations to replace human decision-making and evaluation. Through near-end policy optimization, we update the model parameters. We then apply the model outputs to a congestion negotiation-based router to enhance the quality of simultaneous escape routing. Our method consistently achieves 100% routability in all cases, outperforming other routers that can only complete routing for a portion of the problem.

articleTitle: A CPU-FPGA Based Heterogeneous Accelerator for DNA Sequence Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The BWA-MEM alignment software, known for its efficient algorithm with lower space-time complexity, is extensively used for sequence alignment in low-cost, high-throughput second-generation sequencing. However, the computationally intensive task of the Smith-Waterman (S-W) algorithm accounts for over 50% of the runtime, highlighting a significant performance bottleneck. In this work, we have designed an accelerator for the S-W algorithm using Verilog, focusing on three main optimization strategies: 1) Implementing a ping-pong buffering structure to hide memory access latency during batch processing. 2) Designing an accelerator capable of adapting to any size of scoring matrix computation based on a one-dimensional systolic array. 3) Proposing a Processing Element (PE) reuse strategy to enhance the utilization rate of PEs and devising a dual-pointer control scheme to simplify PE control. We integrated this accelerator into a CPU-FPGA heterogeneous system, significantly enhancing BWA-MEM software performance through CPU and FPGA synergy. Additionally, we developed a CPU-GPU heterogeneous system for comparative analysis employing a similar strategy. In the CPU-FPGA system, the systolic array, incorporating 32 PEs, achieved an 85% PE utilization rate and an 18.27x acceleration ratio.

articleTitle: Repair of H+ Implantation Induced Defects in SiC Single Crystal Film Fabricated by Crystal-Ion-Slicing Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The heterogeneous composite substrates based on SiC single-crystal film fabricated by CIS (Crystal-Ion-Slicing) technology can serve as excellent material platforms for electronic devices with specific functions. Although CIS technology is considered to retain the good material properties of the original material, the defects induced by ion implantation remain significant. Therefore, repairing implantation damage is crucial for further enhancing the material properties. In this study, the morphology, distribution, and rep arability of H+ implantation induced defects were investigated. The research demonstrates that a high concentration of H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> exists on the film surface. On one hand, H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> disrupts the lattice under high-temperature annealing. on the other hand, it thermally diffuses inward, forming energy level defects and causing secondary damage to the crystal. Additionally, the research confirmed that vacancy defects in the deeper layers of the film can be repaired, whereas the high-density defect clusters in the near-surface region cannot be completely repaired. Therefore, a dam-age removal process based on the surface high-density defect distribution is necessary before high temperature annealing. The research methodology in this paper is considered applicable for guiding the development of defect repair processes for various single-crystal films prepared using CIS technology, to better enhance the performance of the transferred film materials.

articleTitle: Formal Verification and Verilog Code Generation for Coq-based Carry-Lookahead Adder Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article describes the application of customized proof techniques for proving theorems related to arithmetic circuits in the Coq theorem prover and generating Verilog code from Coq. By illustrating the correctness verification process of a carry-lookahead adder (CLA) as an example, this set of proof strategies not only significantly simplifies the proof process but also enhances the efficiency of Coq formal verification in general. It is also possible to generate Verilog code for CLA of arbitrary size (up to 128 bits) based on Signal type. Additionally, the Verilog code for CLA generated from Coq can be run directly, has been synthesized and simulated in Quartus.

articleTitle: Research Review of Organic Semiconductor Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Organic power semiconductors have been widely used in flexible electronic devices and other fields due to their flexibility and low manufacturing costs. However, in the field of power applications, the thermal and electrical stability of organic materials is poor, resulting in unreliable device performance. This article elaborates on the working mechanism of organic semiconductors and summarizes their current development status from three aspects: device structure, organic materials, and preparation methods. The future development direction is to improve the voltage resistance and thermal stability of organic transistors through higher performance structural design, higher mobility materials, and higher quality manufacturing methods. These works have great engineering guidance significance for engineers in related fields.

articleTitle: An Automatic Extraction and Verification Method of Security Properties for Integrated Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Formal verification methods can prove whether a integrated circuit(IC) design satisfies desired properties with higher verification efficiency than traditional testing methods. However, it requires manual specification of assertion properties for circuit design, where the quality and completeness of properties are difficult to guarantee. In this work, we propose an automatic extraction and verification method for typical security properties of integrated circuit design based on information flow analysis. An information flow model is constructed for the integrated circuit design. Then, the simulation trajectory of the model is further analyzed to identify information flow behaviors related to confidentiality and integrity. These behaviors are described as information flow security properties. The Yosys verification tool is used to formally verify the extracted information flow properties using its Boolean satisfiability problem (SAT) solver. The results of formal verification can demonstrate that the design satisfies the properties, or in case of property verification failures, quickly locate design vulnerabilities from counterexamples provided by the verification tool. This method facilitates subsequent analysis or vulnerability code refactoring for verification personnel.
